Acquisition order therefore tracks abstraction from the acoustic surface, not the segmental/suprasegmental distinction, extending to prosody an account established for phonetic, lexical and syntactic structure; the no-switch wav2vec 2.0 shows no comparable re-localization.

papers.title: Augur: An Online Learning-based Hardware Data Prefetcher using Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Machine-learning-based hardware prefetchers can learn complex access patterns, but practical deployment demands online adaptation, low-latency inference, and modest hardware cost. We present Augur, a hardware delta prefetcher based on next-generation reservoir computing (NGRC) that meets all three requirements. Augur formulates delta prediction as a history-based regression problem. It constructs a fixed-size reservoir from hashed delta features over a short context window and predicts the next delta using a single dot product. The model is updated online via one-step SGD and requires no offline pre-training, no per-benchmark tuning, and no floating-point arithmetic. Replacing the integer multiplications traditionally used to generate nonlinear reservoir features with bitwise AND operations removes all feature-generation multipliers with no loss in performance. Because Augur regresses a continuous delta, it needs no action set chosen offline for a fixed set of workloads. Augur pairs the reservoir with a simple Markov-based delta predictor for simple delta patterns, and with a selective issuance policy that filters and throttles wasteful prefetches; this policy accounts for about 40% of Augur's advantage and also improves Pythia. Evaluated on 169 traces spanning GAP, Ligra, PARSEC, SPEC CPU 2006, SPEC CPU 2017, and AI workloads, Augur outperforms the state-of-the-art ML-based delta prefetcher by 2.9%, 4.5%, and 5.3% in geomean speedup on 1-, 4-, and 8-core systems, respectively, while achieving ~2x higher prefetch accuracy and 37.8 percentage points fewer overpredictions. Augur is practical to implement at 33 KB storage, 0.32 sq. mm area, and 32.7 mW in 12 nm.

papers.title: Tunnels: Compressing the Solution Subgraph of Regular Path Queries
papers.abstract: Regular path queries (RPQs) are increasingly expected to return the paths that match them, not only their endpoints. Since the number of matching paths can be exponential or infinite, a standard way to deliver them (PMR) is the subgraph $\Hs$ of the product between the graph and the query automaton that contains exactly the nodes lying on some solution path. We show that $\Hs$ can be compressed much further when the graph is available to the decoder: most of $\Hs$ can be regenerated by re-running small parts of the traversal, and only the places where the traversal would waste significant effort on dead branches need to be stored. We formalize this as \emph{tunnels}: regions of $\Hs$ that are re-expanded from a stored entry point with a bounded amount of extra work, either an absolute budget or one proportional to the output produced. We handle the three classes of RPQs: constant-to-variable, constant-to-constant, and variable-to-variable. In the latter, we study the combination of tunnels with cutting the query at a selective articulation point of the automaton and encoding the answer as a union of Cartesian products of leftward and rightward traversals. Our experimental results show improvements of 2 to 3 orders of magnitude over the baseline space of PMR, for an acceptable increase in traversal time.

papers.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
papers.abstract: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback--Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy--security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy--security trade-off in practical scenarios.

papers.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
papers.abstract: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which Gemini 4 agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 2.57x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 12x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

papers.title: Multipole Decomposition of Moving Sources
papers.abstract: Cartesian multipole moments are widely used to analyze and engineer radiation, but the usual relations for their radiated fields assume a wavevector-independent source frequency. For moving sources, Doppler shifts make the frequency depend on the wavevector, so the radiated fields predicted from the moments generally carry errors proportional to v/c. From charge conservation in the laboratory frame, we derive a multipole decomposition of moving sources that retains the usual moments but evaluates their contributions at Doppler-shifted wavenumbers and adds a convection-current term. Requiring no rest frame, it applies to moving matter and to excitation patterns in synthetic motion through media at rest, including superluminal ones. The decomposition also extends to nonuniform translation and to nonrigid patterns with curved spectral supports. Exact calculations for moving electric, magnetic, and toroidal dipoles confirm the decomposition and attribute the different radiation of a dipole in moving matter and in synthetic motion to the laboratory moments that each kind of motion induces. For an anapole, these moments decide whether it radiates. An anapole carried by uniformly moving matter remains nonradiating, whereas an excitation pattern with the same electric and toroidal dipoles radiates in synthetic motion. The decomposition thus makes multipolar analysis available for moving matter and for excitation patterns in synthetic motion, and it opens the way to designing their radiation.

papers.title: Beyond the Pseudo-Inverse: GIM Precoding for Per-Antenna Power Minimisation in MU-MIMO
papers.abstract: We study linear precoder design for multi-user MIMO downlink under per-antenna power constraints (PAPC), which arise naturally when each antenna port has its own power amplifier. While the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse is the unique optimal generalized inverse for zero-forcing precoding under a total power constraint [1], we prove this optimality does not extend to the MMSE/RZF case under PAPC. Any precoder in the Generalized Inverse Matrix (GIM) family shares the same effective channel and per-user SINRs as the pseudo-inverse baseline, while its null-space component reshapes the per-antenna power profile. This separation principle enables minimising peak per-antenna power at fixed SINR targets with zero SINR penalty. We characterise the convex peak-power problem over this family and its active-set optimality, establish MRT and ZF asymptotic limits, and provide a convergent first-order subgradient algorithm. Simulations with 8-64 antennas confirm gains of 1.9-3.7 dB over pseudo-inverse RZF, with GIM-MMSE eliminating essentially all PAPC violations up to 20% per-antenna budget imbalance. The framework applies directly to fully-digital massive MIMO. Cell-free and hybrid analog-digital arrays are promising extensions.

papers.title: A Bridge from Paste to Place: Physics-Guided One-Step Image Composition via Object-Scene Interaction
papers.abstract: Realistic image composition makes a pasted object appear naturally present in a scene while preserving the pasted layout and fine foreground and background details. Reference-based insertion methods preserve overall object identity but can alter pose and fine details, often at substantial computational cost. Foreground harmonization and shadow generation address individual aspects of this task, but neither alone ensures natural integration. An efficient, unified solution remains an open challenge, and large-scale, high-quality datasets and benchmarks for this task are lacking. To address these challenges, we introduce Paste2Place, an end-to-end, physics-guided flow-based model that learns a direct latent bridge from pasted inputs to realistic composites, guided by image-space corrections analytically derived from predicted physical components of object and scene appearance changes. To support training and evaluation, we introduce P2P-Data with 86K manually reviewed synthetic and real-scene training pairs, including dense physical annotations from our Blender rendering and validation pipeline for the synthetic subset. P2P-Bench combines paired compositions and manually pasted inputs from collected images into 1.5K examples for evaluating composition under user-chosen placements. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that Paste2Place achieves substantial advantages in image composition quality and inference speed across diverse scenarios.

papers.title: Complement Cancellation and the Spectral Characterization of Three-Point Recurrence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate both two-sided and one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence within the framework of weakly mixing measure-preserving systems. As our principal result, we establish an exact spectral characterization for the failure of two-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence: namely, a subset \(R\subseteq\mathbb N\) fails to possess this property if and only if there exist a continuous symmetric probability measure \(σ\) on \(\mathbb T\) and a constant \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying \[ 2\widehatσ(n)+\widehatσ(2n)\leq-\varepsilon \qquad(n\in R). \] Our proof of the necessity relies upon a complement-symmetrized correlation identity, whereas the converse is achieved through a construction involving a stationary Gaussian system, a bounded odd observable, Hermite expansions, and an independent Bernoulli extension. Furthermore, we extend this characterization to three-point polynomial configurations as well as to actions of countable abelian groups. In addition, we derive an unconditional analogue in which arbitrary symmetric probability measures take the place of continuous ones, thereby demonstrating a strict separation between the ergodic and weakly mixing classes of recurrence. Subsequently, we turn our attention to the distinction between two-sided and ordinary one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence. It is shown that a suitable negative spectral condition compels the failure of one-sided recurrence. More remarkably, we construct an explicit weakly mixing system wherein the quadratic spectral expression remains uniformly positive, yet the presence of a negative cubic correlation still induces a one-sided recurrence deficit. Consequently, it follows that two-point spectral data alone are insufficient to govern one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence.

papers.title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music
papers.abstract: Large public datasets have driven recent progress in machine learning, from text and vision to speech and general audio. Music remains an outlier, as copyright blocks redistribution of training audio, in particular for modern tasks that need individual stems rather than mixtures. Existing multitrack resources trade off realism, scale, and licensing, as synthetic alternatives rely on proprietary VSTs or naive open rendering that yields weak stems. We introduce SPDMX, an openly-licensed stem corpus rendered from the public-domain PDMX dataset. SPDMX comprises $5{,}469$ song-hours ($2{,}734$ song-hours, or $34.8\%$, of which are multitrack scores) at $44.1$ kHz under CC BY 4.0, with paired MIDI and identifiers that link our dataset to PDMX's original metadata. To our knowledge, SPDMX's multitrack subset constitutes the largest openly-licensed synthetic multitrack subset by song-hours. We then demo SPDMX as a dataset for both source separation and transcription, showing how its increased scale can enable better training of models on synthetic data. We release SPDMX, as well as the open creation pipeline for reuse on other symbolic music datasets.

papers.title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
papers.abstract: Clients and proxies in front of an LLM engine retry calls that time out. After a transient overload, these retries can keep the engine from recovering even when calls arrive below its capacity. Since the engine may keep computing for clients that have left, propagating cancellation looks like the natural remedy. In this paper, we test it on vLLM with overload experiments on three open models, and with scheduler traces of one that follow each client attempt to the execution it creates in the engine. We find that with retries on, cancellation alone did not restore service in any run, and only 12-38% of the calls that arrived after the overload were delivered. The traces suggest why: retries that vLLM ran typically started prefill less than half a second before they timed out. Executions that vLLM later aborted took 79-85% of the prompt tokens it computed, and vLLM's prompt-token counter missed a third to half of all computed prompt tokens. A retry budget restored service by shedding retries but left many of the overload's calls undelivered. Request coalescing delivered every call from the overload onward, some late, unless cancellation had already aborted the running execution. Overload controls should thus be judged by the executions that retries add and the calls that clients receive.

papers.title: Physical Sensing Verification for Cognitive ISAC against UAV Spoofing via Digital Twins
papers.abstract: As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets 5G and 6G base stations detect drones, software agents will act on these detections, so a replayed signal can plant a phantom drone that triggers real actions. This paper proposes a wall-based physical check for such cognitive ISAC systems. A digital twin (DT) predicts the delay and angle of a genuine target's wall echo. A relay can fake the direct echo's range but, standing elsewhere, not the direction of its own wall echo. The paper proves that line-of-sight beam steering cannot expose a matched relay, and that, under stated conditions, a single-antenna relay faking a wall echo leaves a telltale echo where a genuine target leaves none. In a pre-registered ray-tracing study, the twin's evidence separated genuine targets and replays perfectly (AUC 1.000), and a later-registered passive check without extra transmission accepted every held-out genuine target and no replay. The primary active probe was inconclusive (5.3% false acceptances against a 5% limit), lacking threshold margin. At the evaluated relay positions, the conditional bound certifies 3 of 24 held-out streets against adaptive or fixed single-antenna relay signals meeting its conditions, reproduced on fresh streets. Doubling the bandwidth raises this to 11 of 24.

papers.title: How Finite Brains Generalize Without Bound: Spatial Memory as a Universal Computer
papers.abstract: A child who learned to add small numbers adds numbers of any length. LSTMs and Transformers trained on short sequences fail on longer ones. We trace this to what learners read when deciding. A position, count or time takes new values as input grows: it is a coordinate, and a learner that reads one meets in every long input values its experience never covered. Whether two things are the same has the same two answers at every size: it is a coincidence, and a learner that reads only coincidences finds in a long input nothing that short inputs lacked, so finite experience fixes its rule for every size. The memory carries the size of the input and the rule stays finite, and this determines the memory a generalizing brain can have: a memory that grows while what the learner reads of it stays finite has to look the same from every place, so it is made of cycles, and the past is reached by asking what happened when the cycles last stood where they stand now. The cycles are the grid modules, the cells that detect their return the place cells, the records the hippocampal index; a prefrontal controller moves the cycles and never sees them. Reading only coincidences costs no power: what finite experience fixes in such a learner is what Turing machines compute in step with their input, which is why a circuit that evolved to find the way home can learn arithmetic and grammar. In a network of neurons this machine of cycles is the dynamics seen through its symmetry, and symbols are its invariants. Trained on strings up to 40 symbols, the machine solves five benchmark tasks that no LSTM or Transformer solves, among them duplication and binary addition, and beyond the reach of its cycles it fails on the curve the theory predicts. Given larger cycles after training, a machine that saw no string longer than five symbols reverses a string of a million without error. Its controllers run unchanged on neurons.

papers.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Tool-using agents act on email, files, and payments, so an instruction hidden in a web page or a shared document can make an agent send data or money to an attacker. Many runtime defenses put a language model on the decision that lets an action through, so the decision depends on a model that may read the attacker's text and adds model calls to every step. Provenance defenses keep the model off the final check but need a model to plan or route each task first. Where an action goes can instead be read from the tools' typed returns: an email's sender or a payment's account arrives in a typed field, while injected instructions arrive as free text. SPILLWAY turns this observation into a deterministic floor with no per-task plan. The check admits a call when each target value that appears in tool output but not in the user's task was returned by a read-only tool in a typed field or is covered by a fixed delegation rule. A deterministic sanitizer removes instruction-like regions its fixed rules match before the model reads them and retains the removed spans as evidence, and a local judge may restore a refused call, never one whose target lies in the removed text. Across three backbones, and seven task suites on one of them, no standard templated injection redirects an action to an attacker's target under SPILLWAY, at the highest observed mean utility and composite scores (NRP, ERS) of the defenses we run under that attack. A forged chat template also produces a raw zero, and mean in-scope attack success under a released reinforcement-learning attacker is .005. SPILLWAY reaches this floor with no defense-triggered backbone re-run and almost no added model call. As personal AI agents act on users' email, files, and payments, SPILLWAY gives them an auditable refusal floor on where their actions go that keeps them useful and holds across backbones.

papers.title: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. Our main result concerns products of convex bodies. Each block contains an inner ball and lies in a concentric outer ball. The inner radii have a common positive lower bound, and each outer radius is at most a fixed multiple of the corresponding inner radius. This class includes common constraints such as balls and boxes. On each prescribed feasible set of dimension $d$ in this class, every deterministic algorithm using a local oracle needs $\exp(Ω(d))$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case at fixed, sufficiently small accuracies $δ$ and $ε$. The objective Lipschitz and initial objective-value gap bounds are fixed, and each constructed function has a global minimizer in the interior of the feasible set. For broader classes of constraints, supplementary results show that every deterministic algorithm needs $Ω(ε^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsimε^{-2}$ and $δ\lesssimε$. The constants depend on the interior-ball radius and, for inequalities, the local Lipschitz and Slater bounds. These supplementary results cover closed sets that are star-shaped with respect to a ball and convex coercive inequalities with a Slater point, and hold even for convex objectives.

papers.title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
papers.abstract: Spatial agents must interpret observations, maintain consistent spatial memory and make decisions over long interactions. We use Pac-Man as a testbed to study the training challenges behind these capabilities in a Qwen3.5-9B-based agent. Our research trajectory progresses from primitive-action RL on text-based mazes to visual inputs with an internal-state-assisted harness, then toward observation-driven memory and joint policy--harness improvement. The main analysis focuses on text-based maze RL; supplementary sections report visual-adaptation and harness experiments and discuss subsequent directions. Text-based maze RL requires curriculum and training-recipe design to overcome cold starts; normal-start clear rates on eight held-out mazes rise from 0% to a peak of 81.25%. In the second step, model adaptation and harness improvements raise the clear rate from 26.6% to 96.9% on one fixed map with three extra lives. These results highlight three development lessons: use curricula to address cold starts, establish visual grounding before language adaptation, and treat harness design as a determinant of agent performance. They provide practical guidance for subsequent VLM training and spatial-agent development.

papers.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
papers.abstract: Four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed symmetry sector. We determine the spatial cost of recovering it from arbitrary preselected physical spins, allowing unrestricted joint decoding. In the infinite-chain limit followed by increasing defect separation, vanishing error under linear spin budgets requires filling the central gap and at least one outer gap in density. The shorter three-defect interval attains the sharp leading cost through single-spin measurements and classical feedforward. Near-minimal successful supports approach a shortest such span in density. Below this cost, a benchmark finite-ring budget window separates entanglement-breaking connected access from entanglement-preserving single-gap perforations. For a selected two-component family, single-spin Pauli measurements and a one-way classical message yield a scale-stable Bell recovery advantage. The output channel supports positive transmission rates over independently prepared blocks, with coding performed at fixed geometry before the ordered spatial limits. Collective fusion records in discarded spins bound recovery from above, while conjugate retained records certify coherence. Finite-ring examples show that Bell-optimal one-qubit compression can reduce the full output's capacity. On two uncoupled chains with independent bulk states, a repetition embedding raises the leading cost. A matched interacting Ashkin--Teller ladder retains finite-ring geometric separation at every finite nonnegative coupling. The results distinguish useful quantum access from vanishing-error recovery and connect both to critical many-body statistics.

papers.title: Performance Portability of Out-of-Kernel Optimizations on GPUs: A Molecular Docking Case Study
papers.abstract: Achieving performance portability is challenging for irregular scientific applications built as repeated multi-kernel GPU pipelines, because throughput depends on out-of-kernel decisions as much as on kernel efficiency. Using molecular docking as a representative case study, we propose an out-of-kernel tuning methodology that treats batching policy, worker concurrency, and per-worker memory allocation as explicit optimization parameters, replacing backend-dependent occupancy-driven choices with a more portable execution strategy based on explicit resource bounds. We implement this methodology in the muDock mini-app under a manager/worker execution model where multiple host workers share a GPU through independent streams. We then evaluate the methodology on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs across CUDA, HIP, and SYCL implementations. Across all evaluated platform/backend pairs, the memory-bounded formulation exceeds the peak throughput of the occupancy-guided baseline. The fully tuned methodology improves the end-to-end throughput on all tested configurations, achieving an average speedup of 1.53x over the baseline.

papers.title: Frank Elastic Constants of Associating Rigid-Rodlike Systems
papers.abstract: Frank elastic constants of associating rigid rodlike systems are investigated using a mean field theory combined with the Straley elastic free energy formalism. Incorporating the aggregation equilibrium and size-dependent orientational ordering, we analyze the concentration and temperature dependences of the elastic constants for both a monomer--dimer model and a fully polydisperse rodlike aggregate model. We find that aggregation selectively enhances the bend elastic constant through the long-tailed volume fraction distribution, resulting in pronounced elastic anisotropy, $K_{33}\gg K_{11}>K_{22}$. Decreasing temperature or increasing concentration promotes the formation of long rodlike aggregates and induces a rapid increase in the bend elasticity, while the relation $K_{11}=3K_{22}$ remains unchanged.

papers.title: Anchored Slice Propagation with Boundary Transport for 3D CT Segmentation from Three Orthogonal Annotated Slices
papers.abstract: Sli2Vol propagates a binary mask through affinities between adjacent slices, but an error can persist because each prediction becomes the input to the next step. Three orthogonal annotations reduce dependence on any one chain, yet they offer more than three starting masks: where a chain crosses another annotated plane, the correct label is already known. Those labels could correct drift during propagation and indicate how much to trust each chain at fusion. Between annotated planes, the information carried by the chain may matter as well. A binary mask records foreground membership but discards distance to the boundary, a cue that could help follow gradual shape changes between slices.We address these two sources of error with a fixed pretrained affinity backbone. We anchor each chain by correcting its prediction where it crosses another annotated plane, then use its agreement with those labels to weight fusion. We compare this anchored mask with two ways of transporting boundary geometry: a truncated signed-distance field (SDF) propagated by dense affinity averaging, and a contour whose vertices follow motion cues from the same affinity. The contour tracker starts from a hand-crafted rule and learns a motion correction from supervoxel pseudo-objects in 506 CT volumes, without manual organ labels. On 2,091 held-out structure instances from approximately 403 CT scans spanning 17 abdominal structures, anchoring raises mean Dice from 0.737 with orthogonal mask propagation to 0.769 and improves every structure. Beyond the anchored mask, learned contour tracking improves Dice by 5.7\% for the esophagus and 5.9\% for the postcava, while SDF transport improves right-adrenal Dice by 2.8\%. The anchored methods have similar mean Dice (0.769--0.772); contour tracking performs worse on the kidneys, stomach, and hepatic vessel tree. https://github.com/tushaarkataria/AnchoredSlicePropagation

papers.title: The N-soliton solution formula for the Kaup--Kupershmidt equation
papers.abstract: An explicit formula is presented for the $\mathbf N$-soliton solution to the Kaup--Kupershmidt equation, for any positive integer $\mathbf N,$ by using the input data set consisting of $\mathbf N$ distinct positive $p_j$-values and $\mathbf N$ arbitrarily chosen positive $c_j$-values. The formula is derived from the solution to the inverse scattering problem for a third-order linear operator in the reflectionless case with the $p_j$-values related to the bound-state poles of a transmission coefficient and the $c_j$-values related to the bound-state dependency constants. It is indicated how the formula is constructed from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert problem and from the solution to a Marchenko integral equation used in the formulation of the aforementioned inverse scattering problem.

papers.title: Krylov meets Fock: Complementary lenses on quantum dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum dynamics in Krylov space can be represented by a particle hopping on a chain whose sites are the Krylov basis vectors. The goal of this work is to extend this idea to the Fock basis, which in turn allows the description of a generic dynamics in terms of a more general, possibly higher-dimensional lattice. This construction has been dubbed the Fock state lattice (FSL), since its sites are identified with Fock states. To analyze the dynamics on the FSL we introduce various measures of the spread of a state, comparing them among themselves and with their Krylov counterparts. We apply our analysis to two models of light-matter interaction studied in quantum optics: the multi-mode Jaynes-Cummings and the Dicke models. We find that, whenever the FSL is not a chain, the corresponding dynamics provides insights complementary to the Krylov space analysis and, in some instances, greater analytical control. For example, we obtain analytical results for the FSL spread measures of the Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit and determine that their scaling in time detects the superradiant phase transition.

papers.title: On the Onsager--Machlup functional of the infinite-dimensional angular central Gaussian distribution and related measures
papers.abstract: The Onsager--Machlup functional of a probability measure is a generalisation of the negative logarithm of the probability density function, defined precisely using the ratios of masses of balls in the limit of vanishing radius. It plays an important role in several areas of applied mathematics because its minimisers can be understood as modes of the measure. We show that the Onsager--Machlup functional of the angular central Gaussian measure on the unit sphere $\mathcal{S}$ of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space---i.e., the radial projection of a centred Gaussian measure with covariance operator $C$---is constant on the finite-dimensional subsphere of $\mathcal{S}$ spanned by the eigenvectors of leading eigenvalue under $C$, and takes the value $+\infty$ elsewhere. We discuss the consequences of this extreme concentration of mass for maximum a posteriori estimation in Bayesian inverse problems with an angular central Gaussian prior.

papers.title: Deterministic Uniformization for Estimation and Latent Trajectory Inference in Interval-Censored Multistate Transition Models
papers.abstract: Interval-censored multistate data arise when subjects are observed at irregular visit times, leaving transition times and intermediate states unobserved. Likelihood-based inference for continuous-time Markov models often requires computationally intensive matrix exponential evaluations. We propose a deterministic uniformization expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for parameter estimation and latent trajectory inference. By representing the continuous-time process through an embedded Markov chain indexed by latent Poisson event counts, the method enables deterministic E-step calculations without repeated matrix exponential evaluations. The M-step reduces to transition-specific Poisson regressions with exposure offsets, accommodating covariate-dependent transition intensities. We establish uniform truncation error bounds and show that the procedure is an asymptotically monotone generalized EM algorithm. Under standard regularity conditions, the estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal. Simulations demonstrate accurate estimation and computational advantages over direct likelihood optimization, particularly for complex transition structures. We also develop an exact dynamic programming method to calculate posterior probabilities of candidate latent pathways and identify the most probable pathway between observations. Posterior expected transition counts and state occupancy times provide additional subject-specific summaries, while expected-count ratios offer a computational shortcut for classification in simple mutually exclusive pathway structures. The framework supports both population-level inference and individualized characterization of disease progression.

papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Predicting Startup Stress Growth and Strain Hardening in Wormlike Micellar Solutions
papers.abstract: Wormlike micellar solutions exhibit formulation-dependent nonlinear startup responses, including stress overshoot, undershoot, and strain hardening, making prediction across compositions and shear rates challenging. We developed a multi-fidelity machine-learning framework to predict stress-growth curves in cetylpyridinium chloride (CPyCl)-based wormlike micelles from sparse experimental measurements. The framework combines a low-fidelity analytical model describing the overall startup response with high-fidelity experimental data capturing formulation-specific nonlinear features. This approach addresses the limited and uneven coverage of salt chemistry, concentration, and shear rate without relying solely on data-intensive neural-network training. The trained model predicts complete stress-growth responses at untested shear rates and enables extraction of strain-hardening characteristics from interpolated curves. By augmenting sparse rheological measurements, the framework provides a basis for exploring relationships among formulation variables, linear viscoelastic properties, and nonlinear startup behavior, while supporting more efficient characterization of wormlike micellar solutions.

papers.title: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not scalar-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in[0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.

papers.title: NitiBench+: A Temporal Thai Legal Question Answering Benchmark Across 17 Domains
papers.abstract: Law changes over time. A court decides a case under the law in force on that day, and legal QA benchmarks grade answers against today's law. We checked 156,650 decisions of four Thai courts. Up to 67% of them cite law that has since been amended or repealed. We introduce Nitibench+, the sequel of our NitiBench, a Thai legal QA benchmark with 1,670 items across 17 domains, built from decisions of three courts. For each cited section it holds both the text in force on the decision date and the current text, and its retrieval corpus holds every dated version of every Thai statute section. Answers are graded on the Thai Bar Council rubric, the Bar-standard score, and on the overlap between the cited sections and the court's. The report has two parts. Part I measures the cost of the wrong text on 13 open-weight models. Reading the current text of amended law drops the Bar-standard score by 0.25 and missing repealed law drops it by 0.79. The penalty comes from rule changes, 0.45 on the 428 rule-changed items and none on the 331 wording-only items, and Citation F1 does not see it. The text in force is the fair setting. Part II benchmarks today's models on that setting. A public leaderboard ranks 33 models on a held-out test split of 500 items stratified by domain, with a validation split of the same shape released for public use, from memory alone, with the court's sections provided, and as a retrieval agent over the law in force, with the cost per item and the hallucinated citations. The best model scores 7.78 out of 10 and the best open-weight model 6.39. Without a search tool only five open-weight models recall any Thai law, and with it 27 of the 33 models gain and six lose. Leaderboard will take new models as they are released. Legal benchmarks must track dates, and on the right text today's models still leave a wide gap on Thai law.

papers.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ norm and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
papers.abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).

papers.title: Progressive Multi-Scale Super-Resolution via Cascaded Bicubic Anchors and Inter-Scale Mutual Refinement
papers.abstract: Super-resolution networks are trained for one magnification factor, so several output resolutions require several models. We propose PMS-SR, a progressive single-input multiple-output network that produces x2, x4, and x8 results in one forward pass, with a Transformer backbone on the low-resolution grid. In Stage 1, each scale is predicted as a residual over the detached bicubic upsampling of the previous scale's prediction. With Dirac and zero initialization, training starts exactly from the bicubic cascade, and each head adds only the band the previous scale lacks. In Stage 2, inter-scale mutual refinement couples the scales in both directions through space-to-depth feedback, deformable alignment, and per-pixel fusion, so x8 features refine the x2 output. Trained on DF2K, the 7.95M-parameter model achieves a higher PSNR than every compared multi-scale method at x4 and x8 on all five standard benchmarks. At x8, it outperforms the x8-specific DRN-L on all of them, leads all compared methods on Urban100, and is within 0.13 dB of the best result elsewhere. Against three single-scale SwinIR-M models, PMS-SR uses 22% of the parameters, runs 2.9x faster on BSD100 inputs, and its outputs agree 6.7-12.4 dB more closely. Code and pretrained models will be released at https://github.com/julian135707/PMS-SR upon acceptance.

papers.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs without per-LLM fitting, and no law names the factors that set it. From closed-form expressions of LLM inference's computational and memory-access complexity, we derive the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache and next-token computation cost. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from several families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. SIMPLE explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and higher GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy linearly relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; accuracy rises but energy rises faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x range. Moving to agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x, as both prefill and KV-cache terms grow with input length; prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), but not KV-cache cost, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.

papers.title: VLALagBench: Understanding When and Why VLA Inference Latency Matters
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a promising path toward general-purpose robot manipulation. While inference latency can affect task success in a constantly evolving physical world, the relationship between latency and task success rate remains poorly understood. In this paper, we introduce VLALagBench, a comprehensive benchmark for studying VLA inference latency sensitivity across task types, object speeds, execution modes (synchronous and asynchronous), and VLA policies. Using VLALagBench, we find that even a modest inference latency of 100 ms can nearly halve task success on moving targets, with sensitivity varying substantially across tasks and policies. These differences reflect task-specific requirements for precision and continuous motion. By overlapping inference with action execution, asynchronous execution can recover some of the lost success at the cost of more frequent inference requests. Building on these findings, we develop an empirical model that predicts task success from limited calibration data, achieving root-mean-square prediction errors of only 5.7-7.8% across various VLA policies. Given an inference system's latency and per-robot throughput, these predictions guide the selection of system-specific VLA algorithm configurations to maximize task success. We believe VLALagBench and these findings provide a solid foundation for future robotics algorithm-system co-design.

papers.title: Accelerating LLM Pretraining with Zeroth-Order Curvature on Idle Serving Compute
papers.abstract: LLM pretraining is increasingly compute-intensive, while substantial inference serving compute remains idle during off-peak periods. However, such serving hardware is difficult to use for conventional first-order training due to its memory, networking and other system requirements. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization offers a natural interface to this forward-only compute resource, but its gradient estimates break down in pretraining. Unlike fine-tuning, which can confine updates to a small parameter subspace, pretraining must update every parameter, and the alignment of a ZO gradient estimate with the true gradient shrinks as the number of updated parameters grows. We make a different observation: noisy ZO estimates can still provide useful curvature information, even when they are too inaccurate to serve as gradients. Based on this insight, we propose ZO-Curv, which leverages idle forward-only devices to estimate curvature and uses it to adapt and refine the update used during first-order training, thereby accelerating the process. We provide convergence guarantees that characterize the effect of finite-query curvature estimation. Experiments on LLMs from 125M to 1.5B parameters show that ZO-Curv consistently accelerates pretraining. At 770M parameters, ZO-Curv reaches AdamW's 20K-step validation loss in 3.9 hours instead of 7.5 hours, while achieving a lower final loss of 2.70 versus 2.84 under the same step budget. These results show that idle model serving compute can accelerate LLM pretraining when zeroth-order queries are used to estimate curvature rather than gradients directly.

papers.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be induced by a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},τ)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

papers.title: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
papers.abstract: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. Our experimental results show that AltoPIR outperforms existing CPU-based solutions by up to 50.1x.

papers.title: Three New Phases in the Two-Dimensional Potts Model at Complex Temperature
papers.abstract: The complex-temperature phase structure of the two-dimensional Potts model has remained largely unresolved despite decades of study. Here we determine the complex-temperature phase diagram of the 3-state Potts model, and uncover three gapless phases beyond the familiar ferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases. This is done by combining tensor-network free energies with the Poisson equation to compute the Fisher zero density in the thermodynamic limit. The resulting zero distribution unifies and revises long-standing conjectures on the zero loci, and outlines each phase. One is a non-conformal gapless phase, with an exponentially growing number of low-lying transfer-matrix levels distributed across all momentum sectors. The other two are Luttinger-liquid phases with complex-valued Luttinger parameters related by the Kramers-Wannier duality. At the antiferromagnetic critical point, the Luttinger parameter equals 3, while its limit from the adjacent Luttinger-liquid phase is 6. These findings reveal rich phase structures and unconventional critical behavior in a classical textbook model.

papers.title: LADA: A differential algebra-based simulation package for arbitrary-order charged-particle and light optics
papers.abstract: LADA computes charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps by differential algebra in Python, with run-time order selection validated through order nine. It combines these established map methods with ATIMA-based stopping, straggling and scattering, the GLOBAL, CHARGE and ETACHA charge-state models, EPAX fragmentation, six-dimensional integration through measured or computed RF fields with reference-energy rebasing, and section-wise particle tracking with aperture and RF-window losses. Maps retain analytic dependence on external parameters; contraction with input moments gives beam observables and their sensitivities without particle tracking at each setting. Lattice import from COSY, MAD-X, Xsuite and MIRKO provides per-record status and comparisons with available codes. NumPy is the only required dependency. On the HHT benchmark, where the maps of both codes agree in every coefficient through ninth order, the optional compiled DA kernel on eight cores is 1.5 to 1.6 times faster than COSY at orders 3 to 9. Applications include the SIBAF irradiation facility through CALINA, proton microscopy and beam-line studies at GSI and FAIR.

papers.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
papers.abstract: We study separation points for the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and boundary data compactly supported in space and time. We call a space-time point on the boundary and outside the spatial support of the data a separation point of a velocity component if the component takes both signs on sets of positive measure in every sufficiently small adjacent neighborhood. The main ingredient of the analysis is the explicit representation of the velocity and pressure in terms of the boundary data using the confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, under the regularity and unimodality assumptions, log-concavity of the temporal profile yields a unique separation time for the tangential component at every boundary point with \(|x_i|>1\), while the normal component has exactly two separation times for sufficiently large \(|x'|\). For every nonzero nonnegative temporal profile satisfying the regularity assumption, \(\partial_{x_n}^2w_n(x',0,\cdot)\) has a unique simple zero for \(t>1\) when \(|x'|\) is sufficiently large. We also obtain monotonicity and asymptotic behavior of the separation times and quantitative rates at which the corresponding normal derivatives vanish. For tangential data in \(n\geq3\), a separation time for the parallel component exists precisely when \(\partial_{x_1}R_1'ψ(x')>0\), with \(R_1'\) the first Riesz transform; log-concavity makes the separation time unique. For the remaining components, we also prove existence and uniqueness. In both cases, we derive asymptotic formulas involving spatial moments and the geometry of \(\suppψ\). We determine signs of tangential pressure derivatives and, for radial \(ψ\), establish uniqueness and asymptotics of their zeros.

papers.title: Solvable dynamical model of in-context learning
papers.abstract: Pretrained Transformer architectures display a surprising in-context learning ability without additional training. How the learning process guides the network to achieve this intriguing capability remains unsolved. In this study, we focus on a single-layer single-head linear attention model, where an empirical risk minimization is defined for learning. Given a finite number of training examples, we determine the exact solution of network-parameter dynamics, which is linked to the training error and generalization error, characterizing how memorization and generalization emerge from learning and how these transitions are related to curvatures of the empirical risk landscape. Furthermore, we calculate a data-dependent free energy, from which the training and generalization errors in the long time limit of learning dynamics can be well predicted. Our work adds insights toward understanding the mechanism of in-context learning especially from a learning dynamics perspective.

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson Light Cones in Long-Range Bosonic Systems
papers.abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds formulate emergent causality in quantum many-body dynamics. In this Letter, we study interacting bosonic systems with long-range interactions, in which both the standard assumptions of short-range interactions and uniformly bounded local energy scales are absent. We derive upper and lower bounds whose light-cone exponents depend jointly on the spatial decay $α$ and bosonic interaction order $p$. The key physical mechanism balances enhancement by local boson concentration with coherent amplification of long-range interactions. Our state-transfer protocol realizes this balance by concentrating bosons within mesoscopic blocks while preserving a spatial array of occupied sites. For integer $p\ge4$ and $2d<α\le2d+1$, the leading exponents coincide, determining the optimal light cone under controlled-density assumptions, up to arbitrarily small upper-bound exponent losses. Our results identify a new mechanism for accelerating information propagation through the combined effects of bosonic particle accumulation and long-range interactions.

papers.title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
papers.abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and in practice behaves like an accelerated method. This led to the conjecture that it is uniformly accelerated on strongly convex functions as well. The conjecture is false. Consider exact subspace methods whose memory is a window of recent gradients and steps plus finitely many fixed cumulative sums. Uniform acceleration then requires either a window whose length grows as the square root of the condition number or a sum that forgets at a rate of at least the order of the inverse square root. For one filter pair with a fixed factor and a bounded window this scale of forgetting is necessary and sufficient up to constants. SESOP remembers too much and the plane form of conjugate gradients too little: neither is uniformly accelerated, even on infinitely differentiable functions that are quadratic near the minimizer. A short window, in contrast, converges locally quadratically over blocks of steps when the Hessian is Lipschitz near the minimizer and equals a multiple of the identity plus a low-rank term there. Pairs of geometric filters created at fixed times give a uniformly accelerated method with logarithmic memory and no problem constants, also with inexact subproblems. A single pair with a smoothly adapted factor needs two vectors and is accelerated up to a prefactor polynomial in the condition number.

papers.title: Photon-loss tolerance of the surface-GKP code with anti-photon-loss decoding
papers.abstract: Photon loss somewhat limits fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing. We investigate its effect on finite-energy Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) states by modeling the pure-loss channel directly. We obtain photon-loss threshold estimates for the surface-GKP code using nearest-lattice-point inner GKP decoding and minimum-weight perfect matching for the outer surface code. For GKP states with $ε=0.01$ and $ε=0.05$, corresponding to GKP squeezing of $20$ and $13\,\mathrm{dB}$, the estimated thresholds are $γ^\ast=5.5\%$ ($0.24\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $γ^\ast=5.9\%$ ($0.26\,\mathrm{dB}$), respectively. We then introduce an anti-photon-loss inner decoder that compensates for the contraction of the measured quadrature. It increases the corresponding threshold estimates to $γ^\ast=9.8\%$ ($0.45\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $γ^\ast=6.3\%$ ($0.28\,\mathrm{dB}$). Our results highlight the importance of accounting for loss-induced lattice contraction in inner decoding and demonstrate that quadrature compensation enhances the photon-loss tolerance of surface-GKP codes for both high- and moderate-quality GKP states, providing a route toward more photon-loss-robust optical quantum computing.

papers.title: On Small Universal Reversible Turing Machines
papers.abstract: A reversible Turing machine (RTM) is a Turing machine in which every instantaneous description has at most one predecessor. Writing $\mathrm{URTM}(m,n)$ for a universal RTM with $m$ states and $n$ symbols, we construct $\mathrm{URTM}(3,600)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(4,38)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(5,36)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(6,28)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(7,26)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(8,21)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(9,8)$, $\mathrm{URTM}(10,7)$, and $\mathrm{URTM}(85,2)$; each of them has fewer states or fewer symbols than each of the nine URTMs in Morita's book (2017). Most of them come from improved versions of Morita's conversions to three states, to four states, and to two symbols; for example, the improved conversion to three states uses $O(mn^2)$ symbols instead of $O(m^2n^3)$. $\mathrm{URTM}(10,7)$ comes from merging two states of Morita's $\mathrm{URTM}(13,7)$, recording the difference in tags on the tape cells, and then merging symbols, three times; one more such step gives $\mathrm{URTM}(9,8)$. We also show that the halting problem of RTMs with at most two states is decidable for finite instantaneous descriptions, so that no RTM with at most two states is universal under any notion of universality that reduces the halting problem of Turing machines to it by a computable encoding into finite instantaneous descriptions; in particular, there is no URTM with at most two states in our formalization of Morita's definition. We also show that no three-state, two-symbol RTM is universal in that formalization.

papers.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\mathbb{C}$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
papers.abstract: We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3\to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).

papers.title: Distilling Knowledge from Search: Decoder Model Factory for Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: We introduce GraphMP, a learning-based message-passing decoder for quantum low-density parity-check codes that transfers without fine-tuning across code families, code sizes, physical error rates, and noise models. Its local message passing keeps computation scalable as the decoding graph grows. We further embed GraphMP in a beam-search algorithm that progressively refines candidate error patterns, trading additional decoding time for lower logical error rates. To turn this decoding effort into lasting improvements, we propose the decoder model factory, a paradigm for training successive models on data collected by earlier models during decoding. In our implementation, verified search trajectories provide reusable training data for distilling knowledge into subsequent models. Across generations, the model factory yields a search-enhanced decoder that is broadly competitive with Relay-BP. On the largest code block, which encodes $4612$ logical qubits, it achieves a lower logical error rate and about $20$ times the decoding throughput of the standard Relay-BP baseline. These results motivate a coupled quantum-classical architecture with two interacting cycles: rapid decoding protects quantum information, while slower learning adapts the models to changing noise conditions. The long-term vision is a scalable decoder model factory that continually produces high-performance, low-latency decoders for evolving quantum hardware.

papers.title: Universal quantum control in biorthogonal framework
papers.abstract: As a paradigm for describing the open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation generally modifies the state norm, impeding the coherent control over the system. With a general instantaneous representation spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for finite-dimensional systems under a general time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in both ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of several transitionless passages. Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer, a non-Hermitian holomonic quantum gate implemented in a three-level system, and chiral state conversion. For the bidirectional transfer and the holonomic gate, we can further identify the parametric constraints under which a unitary transformation is formed to link the initial and target states. As a result, the final state is automatically normalized even though the transitional dynamics is nonunitary. In population transfer, controlled gain and loss cut the required coherent pulse area, delivering shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark at equal average Rabi frequency. For the chiral state conversion, we find that a closed parametric loop along opposite directions leads to distinct final state, which is irrelevant to encircling the exceptional point or not. Our work integrates the universal quantum control into the biorthogonal framework, displaying full-rank coherent control in non-Hermitian systems.

papers.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
papers.abstract: Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem: the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. The Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet) is a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain in its architecture, building the event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy and combining all jet assignment hypotheses, evaluated with shared weights, with learned weights. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built in, the network size does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and no generator-level jet assignments are used in training. Developed for the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state and used in several CMS searches, CoReNet with 1508 parameters performs well above kinematic baselines on fast-simulated Higgs boson pair production against QCD multijet events and trains in minutes on a single GPU, and its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most signal events in which it is defined. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, we test the construction on $HH \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-$ against semileptonic $t\bar{t}$, where encoding the decay chain of the background as well improves the classification at a cost of about $10^{3}$ parameters. In both final states, CoReNet performs comparably to a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/cms-cmu/CoReNet.

papers.title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
papers.abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Using two results from Fourier's preprint, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these values of $k$. The second version of Fourier's preprint gives an independent proof of this statement. For $k=1$, the equality statement is false: the polytopes $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have the same number of edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. Together with Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. Our results are formalized in Lean 4, with one result of Fourier's preprint and three published results taken as hypotheses.

papers.title: Central Limit Theorems and Network-Free Inference for Heterogeneous Spatial Autoregressions on Sparse Graphons
papers.abstract: Network dependence is widely regarded as a fundamental obstacle to inference: outcomes linked through a graph are not independent, the graph is rarely observed in full, and models for how dependence propagates are easily misspecified. We show that for a broad class of responses generated through a random network, the obstacle is smaller than it appears. We study a heterogeneous spatial autoregression on a sparse graphon, in which each node's response is a weighted average of its neighbors' responses with a node-specific, nonparametric coefficient plus a node-specific input, and we prove that sample means and smooth functions of vector means are asymptotically Gaussian down to average degree nearly logarithmic in the population size, allowing unbounded graphons with hubs and heavy-tailed inputs. The limiting variance interpolates exactly between two regimes according to the sampling fraction. When the observed nodes are a vanishing fraction of the population, the variance is the marginal variance of the response, the ordinary sample variance is consistent, and the usual $t$-interval is valid with no knowledge of the network. The proof averages over the graph rather than conditioning on it, isolating the behavior of the response through an exact identity for resolvents of Markov kernels and controlling the network noise by an Efron-Stein inequality; neither step requires the walk-by-walk covariance bounds of fixed-network analyses. Consequences for regression with node-level and network-derived covariates are derived.

papers.title: Embedding dense minors via crux
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_α(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $αd$ for any fixed $0<α<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $Ω(\sqrt{d\,C_α(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

papers.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
papers.abstract: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.

papers.title: Homodyne versus heterodyne detection near Gaussian states: Fraction of the quantum Fisher information recovered
papers.abstract: Homodyne and heterodyne detection are the standard measurements of an optical mode. Which of them yields more information is known only for particular tasks, with opposite answers for displacements and tomography. We compare them for every small change of a Gaussian state by their efficiency, the recovered fraction of the quantum Fisher information. We prove that near any Gaussian state of any number of modes the quantum Fisher information and the Fisher information of any Gaussian measurement are sums over the Hermite orders of the change, each term fixed by the covariance matrix and the measurement. A fixed Gaussian measurement measures no change more efficiently than the best displacement. Near a thermal state of one mode closed-form efficiencies reconcile the known comparisons, and homodyne detection at a uniformly random phase recovers at most one half, a bound raised by squeezing. Near a coherent state both detections recover exactly one half for every change of finite quantum Fisher information (the largest possible average). At the two-mode squeezed vacuum, homodyne detection of both modes at uniformly random phases is as efficient as heterodyne detection for every such change. On simulated records of one set of distant states, a likelihood-ratio observer shows a heterodyne advantage under Gaussian noise and none under loss, as the theory predicts. Under dephasing it shows none. Neural networks on reconstructed Wigner functions can show a heterodyne advantage absent from the records. For random non-Gaussian changes of up to seven photons near a thermal state the median efficiencies of both detections lie between 0.04 and 0.19, 5 to 25 times below the optimal measurement.

papers.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
papers.abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

papers.title: CAMR: Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Continual learning requires large language models to acquire new knowledge and capabilities while retaining what they have learned. Fine-tuning and replay support acquisition and retention, but deciding whether incoming examples need supervision and which historical examples to revisit remains a challenge. We propose Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay (CAMR), an adaptive framework that jointly controls current-example supervision and historical replay. CAMR combines compatibility checks with a learned memory gate to guide an online policy over three actions: learning incoming examples with general replay, jointly reinforcing compatible related examples, and skipping direct supervision of verified mastered duplicates. The policy learns from acquisition, retention, and training-cost feedback under a bounded per-arrival replay budget. We evaluate CAMR with Qwen3-8B-Base on continual factual updating and cross-task and cross-domain learning. On WikiBigEdit, CAMR consistently leads evaluated methods in Original Match from 3K to 100K facts, reaching 93.66% after just 3K facts and surpassing Full-history Replay (LoRA) after 100K facts. It also achieves the highest final scores on all four selected TRACE tasks and maintains or improves earlier-task performance relative to post-acquisition levels in a sequence spanning financial question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and summarization.

papers.title: Antenna-coupled microstrip summing network for wave-like dark matter searches
papers.abstract: A commonly used technology for axion and other wave-like dark matter searches is a microwave resonator. In such experiments, the detected signal strength depends on the coupling between the resonator and the microwave transmission line that delivers power to the amplifier. In Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) and other cavity searches, this coupling is typically achieved using a compact wire antenna inserted into the cavity. While this approach is adequate for right-cylindrical cavities, it can become difficult to efficiently extract power from large-volume, multi-wavelength ($V \gg λ^3$) resonators targeted for higher frequencies, such as those designed by ADMX-VERA (Volume Enhanced Resonant Axion). Here, we present a solution based on a microwave slot-antenna array capacitively coupled to a microstrip "summing network," which coherently combines signals from multiple transmission lines into a single output. This summing architecture is adapted from designs originally developed for cosmic microwave background (CMB) detectors. We demonstrate the design and characterization of a new high-frequency resonator that employs this readout scheme in the $19-21$ GHz range. Finally we discuss the potential to reach Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky (DFSZ) sensitivity using multiple summing network cavities fitted into a large volume.

papers.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic not 3
papers.abstract: This article takes place in the extension and generalization proposed by Corredor, Deloro and Wiscons of the works of Dickson and Wagner regarding the Classification of minimal $\text{Sym}(n)$- and $\text{Alt}(n)$-modules. In particular, we classify the minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(6)$-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(n)$- and $\text{Sym}(n)$-modules with an additive dimension.

papers.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Style over Substance? Linguistic Bias in LLM-based Peer Review
papers.abstract: The number of paper submissions to major AI conferences has increased dramatically in recent years, substantially increasing the peer-review workload of researchers. At the same time, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support peer review, both by individual reviewers and by conference organizations. While LLM capabilities have improved considerably, their evaluations may be influenced by linguistic characteristics that are unrelated to scientific content. In this work, we introduce a controlled experimental framework for studying such effects by systematically perturbing the linguistic style of research papers. Specifically, we rewrite papers to exhibit (i) linguistic features associated with native or non-native English writing, and (ii) high- or low-confidence linguistic features. To construct these interventions, we derive fine-grained rewriting instructions grounded in the linguistic literature and apply them using LLMs. Crucially, our interventions are designed to preserve the underlying scientific content. We then evaluate the resulting papers using different LLM reviewers. Our experiments expose a critical vulnerability in LLM-based peer review: reviewers systematically reward confident rhetoric independent of scientific content, raising serious concerns about the robustness of their assessments.

papers.title: PatentAgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents with Professional Patent Task Suites
papers.abstract: Patent practice lies at the intersection of technical, legal, and linguistic work, making it challenging yet crucial to technological innovation. Recently, rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems have demonstrated the potential to complete realistic business workflows and even patent works.
