papers.abstract: Safe reinforcement learning (RL) commonly enforces expected-cost constraints, but such expectation-form safety may fail to control the probability of rare high-cost trajectories. Chance-constrained MDPs (CCMDPs) impose a stronger probability-level requirement, but are widely viewed as harder because the chance constraint itself is nonconvex and depends on the full trajectory rather than a Bellman-linear expectation. In this paper, we reveal that this computational difficulty does not necessarily imply a higher statistical price. For tabular discounted CCMDPs with bounded successor support and access to a certified planning oracle, we establish a model-based upper bound, with a matching lower bound up to logarithmic terms. Technically, our key idea is the \emph{Bellman distributional certificate}, which constructs a Bellman recursion for constraint violation probabilities before policy selection. The certificate reduces trajectory-level safety analysis to local transition uncertainty, avoiding a union bound over the potentially exponential number of candidate policies. For stochastic policies, we give a model-free variance-reduced policy-gradient algorithm with a finite-sample expected KKT-residual guarantee and independent validation of every accepted policy. Numerical experiments on synthetic CCMDPs and an IEEE 14-bus energy storage control benchmark illustrate the safety and mechanism behavior of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Reduction technique for expanding the Feynman diagrams in AdS$_2$
papers.abstract: We formulate the reduction technique for expanding the $n$-point AdS Feynman diagrams in two dimensions into the Wilson line networks. The technique applies to any $n$-point tree diagram, expressing it as several series of the matrix elements of Wilson line network operators, and employs the Wilson network expansions of the $(n-1)$-point AdS$_2$ Feynman diagrams, which can in turn be obtained using the same technique. Consequently, the complexity of this technique does not increase with $n$, provided that the expansions of the $(n-1)$-point diagrams are known. To demonstrate the reduction technique, we apply it to all topologically distinct five-point AdS$_2$ Feynman tree diagrams. The resulting expansions near the conformal boundary reproduce the known decompositions of the corresponding five-point Witten diagrams into conformal blocks.

papers.title: When a better baseline makes delta learning worse: separating residual scale from learnability to guide target design
papers.abstract: In scientific machine learning, $Δ$-learning trains models on residual errors relative to approximate baselines, assuming that smaller residual scales inherently yield better downstream accuracy. Here, we demonstrate that residual scale alone is an insufficient heuristic for learnability. For molecular total energies, replacing a linear baseline with a neural network fitted to the same elemental counts reduced the residual scale, yet more than doubled GemNet's prediction error. Across local structural descriptors, more flexible baselines produced smaller residuals that varied sharply between structurally similar molecules. By contrast, semi-empirical baselines left larger residuals, yet yielded lower test error and improved out-of-domain transferability. Across the targets studied, scale-normalized graph Dirichlet roughness tracked scale-normalized prediction error, suggesting its use as a pre-training diagnostic for target selection. These results motivate baseline complementarity as a target-design principle in scientific machine learning: a useful baseline captures contributions the downstream architecture struggles to predict.

papers.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
papers.abstract: On a compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold, the existence of a strictly positive plurinegative $(1,1)$-current with smooth exterior derivative implies that the canonical bundle is nef, and ample if every positive Lelong upper level set of the current has complex dimension at most two; in dimensions one and two, hyperbolicity alone suffices for ampleness. Next, we study Hermitian metrics of constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature $c$. Locally and without compactness assumptions, any such metric with $c\ne0$ is Kähler in dimension three, on balanced fourfolds, and under rank bounds on the iterated Chern curvature hull of the $(1,0)$ torsion derivative. Globally, on compact manifolds in Fujiki's class, the metric is Kähler--Einstein when $c<0$ and Kähler flat when $c=0$. Without the Fujiki hypothesis, $c=0$ need not imply Chern flatness: for every dimension $n\ge7$, we construct compact balanced nonflat examples with all four Chern--Ricci contractions vanishing. Nevertheless, on a compact Hermitian manifold with $c=0$ and vanishing first Chern--Ricci form, Kähler flatness follows if there exists a smooth semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form positive definite at one point.

papers.title: Spectral synthesis with the complexity parameter in $\mathbb{Z}_N^d$
papers.abstract: We study asymptotic spectral synthesis on $\mathbb Z_N^d$ using the Fourier ratio, the quotient of the counting-measure $\ell^1$ and $\ell^2$ norms of the unitary Fourier transform. For supports of cardinality $N^{α+o(1)}$, the Fourier-ratio concentration exponent satisfies $0\leqκ\leq\fracα{2}$. We prove a finite-scale synthesis estimate that uses either the Fourier ratio of a function or that of its support indicator. In particular, the indicator condition applies uniformly to arbitrary weights on the support. Uniform $\ell^p$ bounds imply decay of the largest Fourier coefficient when $2\leq p<\frac{2(d-2κ)}{α-2κ}$, with every finite $p\geq2$ allowed at maximal concentration. Random unions of cosets show that the finite critical exponent is sharp for every admissible pair in each prescribed ambient dimension, along prime-power moduli. We also determine the exact synthesis constant for sets with a transitive group of affine symmetries. For paraboloids this constant is an explicit divisor sum. The formula proves endpoint synthesis along powers of a fixed odd prime, although the endpoint fails along primes. Along products of distinct small primes, synthesis extends to a larger exponent. These families have the same Fourier-ratio exponent. Finally, we relate Fourier concentration to generalized Salem estimates, additive energy, Fourier algebra norms, and necessary conditions for extension estimates.

papers.title: Spectral divide-and-conquer MCMC for long stationary time series
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference via Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods can be prohibitively slow for long time series. Distributed Bayesian inference across multiple cores or machines is non-trivial since simple data splits in time perform badly under temporal dependence. We show that a systematic partitioning of the periodogram observations in the frequency domain gives a fast and accurate posterior approximation for stationary series that can also be used when the computations exceed the memory capacity of a single computational node. Our method uses the asymptotic independence of periodogram observations in the Whittle likelihood to develop a distributed fast Fourier transform combined with embarrassingly parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms in modern cluster-computing frameworks. We establish that the error of the spectral divide-and-conquer MCMC posterior approximation relative to the exact time-domain posterior converges to zero in probability in a shrinking neighbourhood of the full-data Whittle posterior mode. The proposed method is shown to be competitive with the current state-of-the-art distributed MCMC for time series when dependence is weak, and substantially more accurate in a highly persistent setting. The methodology is used to perform a rolling forecast evaluation of one-second market liquidity costs from histories of up to 24 million observations.

papers.title: Dephasing-Induced Universal Spin Fluctuations in a Localized Hubbard Chain
papers.abstract: Decoherence usually washes out quantum effects. We show that in a disordered chain it can instead switch on universal fluctuations. In the infinite-$U$ Hubbard chain, particles cannot pass one another, so the spin crossing a cut is fixed by the number of particles that cross. Without an environment, disorder localizes the charge and the spin fluctuations stop growing. Dephasing restores diffusion: the spin width grows again as $t^{1/8}$, fastest at an intermediate dephasing rate, and the spin distribution takes the same non-Gaussian M-Wright form as in the clean chain.

papers.title: A finite Livshits theorem and local length spectrum rigidity
papers.abstract: We show that for closed negatively curved Riemannian manifolds whose length spectrum is exponentially separated, the length spectrum is a local isometry invariant. The main tool used in the proof is a finitary version of the Livshits theorem with an exponential tail that improves with the regularity.

papers.title: Charged Klein--Gordon modes on an Ellis wormhole: magnetic confinement and conditional Heun-polynomial solvability
papers.abstract: We study a charged Klein--Gordon field on the complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ellis wormhole, coupled to the pullback of a uniform ambient magnetic field. The induced gauge potential is regular, whereas the intrinsic magnetic pseudoscalar reverses sign across the throat. For $α_B>0$, the radial operator is unitarily equivalent to a self-adjoint one-dimensional Schrödinger operator with a smooth confining potential and discrete spectrum. The radial equation is reduced to confluent-Heun form, and polynomial solvability is shown to require two independent termination conditions. These conditions yield degree-zero Gaussian modes, degree-one states of both global parities, and representative degree-two even states. Exact Ellis-measure normalization is obtained for the degree-zero and degree-one modes. An independent fourth-order full-line finite-difference calculation validates the analytic benchmarks and determines the first eight eigenvalues and their parities. In the double-well regime, the forbidden-region action determines the leading semiclassical exponential of the even--odd level splitting.

papers.title: Optimal Joint Lower Bound for Sparse Quantum Linear System Solvers
papers.abstract: Quantum linear system solvers form one of the central algorithmic primitives in quantum computing, with applications ranging from differential equations and optimization to machine learning. Their cost is commonly measured through query complexity, which counts the number of oracle calls needed to access the input matrix. In the sparse-access model, this complexity is governed by three parameters: the condition number $κ$, the sparsity $s$ of the input matrix, and the target precision $\varepsilon$. The dependence on $κ$ and $\varepsilon$ is already well understood through the lower bound $Ω(κ\log(1/\varepsilon))$, which matches the best known scaling in these parameters. Once the sparsity $s$ is included, however, the expected lower bound has long been conjectured to be $Ω(κ\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. Recent work by Mori et al. [Quantum Sci. Tech. 11 035063 (2026)] made an important step towards this goal by establishing the lower bound $Ω(κ\sqrt{s})$ for constant error $\varepsilon$. In this work, we complete the picture and prove the full joint lower bound $Ω(κ\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in the sparse-access model, thereby establishing the anticipated dependence on all three parameters simultaneously.

papers.title: GameReplica: A Benchmark for Black-Box Visual Game Replication by Vision-Language Agents
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for coding agents typically assess implementation from explicit specifications, leaving open whether agents can discover and reproduce systems whose rules are undocumented and accessible only through interaction. We study this capability in web games, which offer controlled environments with observable actions and outcomes, and introduce GameReplica, a benchmark for end-to-end black-box game replication. It comprises 125 instances spanning 25 web games and five core mechanism families, with each game instantiated at five difficulty levels. Under container isolation, an agent accesses the target game only through an action--screenshot interface, may iterate between probing the game, implementing a replica, and checking it, and delivers a self-contained runnable replica together with a rule checklist. A reference-grounded evaluation then scores the deliverables separately on rule consistency, implementation consistency, and visual fidelity. Experiments across six models and five agent runtimes show that black-box replication remains challenging: Claude Opus 4.8 achieves the highest Overall score, 71.6%, while the other models obtain 4.0%--43.0%. Every model scores highest on visual fidelity and lowest on rule consistency, suggesting that reproducing appearance is easier than recovering mechanics. Difficulty widens the gap: from L1 to L5, the four lower-scoring models show relative Overall score declines of 33%--63%, whereas the strongest model declines by less than 5%. In the evaluated configurations, outcomes vary more across models than across agent runtimes, and most attributed failures of weaker models arise during exploration, before replica code is written. Resources and interactive demonstrations are available at https://qqqqqqby.github.io/GameReplica/.

papers.title: PRIME: Perception Feedback with Situational Memory Embeddings in VLA Models
papers.abstract: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for autonomous driving operate primarily through feedforward inference across the perception--reasoning--planning hierarchy. While modern architectures maintain temporal recurrence within the perceptual module, early perception remains blind to downstream reasoning and navigation goals, processing visual inputs agnostically without prioritizing cues informed by prior decisions. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces PRIME, a learned feedback mechanism that conditions the VLA perceptual queries on a novel Situational Memory. By aggregating latent representations of past perception, reasoning, navigation goals, and predicted behaviors across an L-step window via cross-attention, PRIME enables intent-driven perceptual attention at minimal computational cost, adding only a maximum of 29.7M parameters (0.41% of the 7.3B-parameter base model). Evaluated on the Bench2Drive closed-loop benchmark, PRIME achieves a state-of-the-art Driving Score of 82.47 (+4.73 over ORION) and a Success Rate of 60.00% (+5.38 percentage points), the highest reported Driving Score among published VLAs trained on Think2Drive demonstrations.

papers.title: Norms of Schneider--Teitelbaum Polynomials in $p$-adic Fourier Theory
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and let $P_n(X)$ denote the Lubin--Tate analogues of the binomial polynomials arising in the $p$-adic Fourier theory of Schneider and Teitelbaum. For a particular choice of Lubin--Tate logarithm, we determine explicitly the norms of the functions $P_n(xΩ)$ on the Banach spaces of locally $F$-analytic functions of fixed order, where $Ω$ is a Lubin--Tate period. Our computation is based on a recent valuation formula of Ardakov and Berger for the values $P_n(Ω)$. As an application, we improve the Bannai--Kobayashi normalization of these polynomials. Each element of the resulting basis has norm one.

papers.title: Percolation Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: We study Percolation Markov Decision Processes (PMDPs), where the decision maker repeatedly moves a token through the d-dimensional integer lattice with deterministic transitions and random payoffs assigned to the edges. Payoffs are revealed before the beginning of the decision process and the decision maker aims to maximize the average accumulated payoff over a fixed horizon. First, we address general asymptotic control-theoretic questions by proving the existence of the uniform value and 0-optimal strategies. Furthermore, we examine the structural properties of optimal strategies: we establish the existence of stationary 0-optimal strategies for a class where the token moves in a fixed direction independent of the player's actions, and we provide low-dimensional examples to illustrate their complexity. Moreover, we introduce a dimensional lifting property that allows PMDPs to be approximated by lower-dimensional PMDPs, offering a representation of the approximation of critical probability thresholds in percolation theory via PMDPs.

papers.title: Uniqueness of embedded minimal Lagrangian tori in $\mathbb{CP}^2$
papers.abstract: We prove that any embedded minimal Lagrangian torus in the complex projective plane is congruent to the Clifford torus. This settles the orientable case of Oh's classification conjecture. The proof uses a new two-point function constructed from Hermitian products of normalized horizontal lifts.

papers.title: Rank and computation of the pathlifting Jacobian of a DAG ReLU network
papers.abstract: This paper provides a self-contained proof of the rank of the pathlifting Jacobian of a DAG ReLU network by performing an induction on the network's number of hidden nodes. In fact, the induction is elementary, and the key recipe is to consider the skeleton matrix of the network, a sparse matrix encoding the network paths, and transform the representation of one of its hidden neurons into an output node. The proof relies on intermediate propositions which link the pathlifting, its Jacobian, the network parameters, and its skeleton matrix, which, on top of permitting to conclude on the rank of the pathlifting Jacobian, also provide a way to compute it without backpropagation and whose computation cost is super efficient in practice compare to usual backpropagation. The paper is provided with a Python module that implements the different propositions of the paper for feed forward networks and is used to experimentally quantifies the computational gain of computing the pathlifting Jacobian with the proposed theory.

papers.title: Differential equations for Dotsenko--Fateev integrals: the case of degenerate fields $Φ_{n,1}$
papers.abstract: We study higher-order differential equations corresponding to integrals of the Dotsenko--Fateev type and associated with four-point correlation functions with degenerate fields $Φ_{n,1}$. We determine the general structure and coefficients of the equations in terms of the integral parameters $ \{ A,B,C,g \} $. In particular, special cases of these equations in CFT are used for verification. In addition, the relationship between higher-order differential equations and hypergeometric operators is established.

papers.title: SAiFE-gym: Model-based Environments for Automated Market Making with Concentrated Liquidity
papers.abstract: We present SAiFE_gym, a Python module that provides a collection of simulation environments for studying trading problems in constant product markets (CPMs) with concentrated liquidity (CL). These markets give liquidity providers (LPs) granular control over how their capital is allocated and enable them to adjust their range of liquidity provision dynamically based on market conditions, which in turn determines how they earn fees. We decompose the microstructure of CPMs with CL into interactive components that allow researchers and practitioners to capture various economic settings. We employ a vectorized approach to optimize our environments, making them scalable for high-dimensional reinforcement learning (RL) workflows, suitable for learning dynamic liquidity provision strategies. We demonstrate the benefits of our environments by evaluating the performance of RL agents in CPMs with CL under various market conditions.

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.

papers.title: Evaluating Ambient Clinical Scribes in India: The Need for Multilingual Real-World Clinical Conversation Data
papers.abstract: Ambient clinical scribes (ACS) are being rapidly deployed at scale across Global South healthcare settings to reduce clinicians' documentation time, especially in overburdened environments such as India. These ACS are primarily developed or distilled from models built and validated on Global North speech, languages and consultation styles. Indian clinical encounters are brief, triadic, multilingual, code-mixed with low-resource languages, and conducted in highly resource-constrained, noisy settings -- increasing the likelihood of ASR and note-generation errors manyfold. We argue for a standardized evaluation infrastructure to assess whether these systems are safe, reliable, and well-suited to the Indian healthcare setting. We substantiate our claims through a mixed-methods study -- a systematic survey of publicly available patient-clinician conversational datasets, a quantitative comparison of some simulated datasets against conversational and cultural markers drawn from the Indian clinical-communication literature, and semi-structured interviews with four organizations building and deploying ACS in India. Our survey shows that there are no large-scale, publicly available, real-world benchmarks for ACS in India, with existing datasets being overwhelmingly synthetic or simulated. We note that amongst the available simulated datasets that we compare, the Global North datasets diverge significantly from the expected conversational and cultural structures of their Indian encounters. Finally, our interviews reveal that deploying organizations have each built proprietary, incomparable evaluation pipelines, creating a fragmented ecosystem with no independent and reliable basis for procurement. We call for the development of a publicly shared, real-world, multilingual benchmark for ACS evaluation and outline the properties and policies such a benchmark would require.

papers.title: Equilibrium selection and sharp convergence rates for a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with simplex-volume interactions
papers.abstract: We study a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. The associated free energy is not isplacement semiconvex when the simplex dimension $n$ is at least two. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a noncompact continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. The limit is then selected by the initial covariance, whose eigenvectors and eigenvalue gaps are preserved by the flow. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates. For compactly supported initial data with nonstationary covariance, the sharp rate is the smaller of the covariance relaxation rate and three times the slowest transport rate, provided that the third moments do not vanish along the directions of slowest transport. The skewness of the initial datum, rather than its covariance, may therefore dictate the long-time behavior.

papers.title: Regular Expression Matching with Ordered Linear Backreferences
papers.abstract: A regular expression with backreferences (rewb) specifies a set of strings formed by characters combined with concatenation, union, star operators, and backreferences. A backreference consists of a capturing group $(\cdot)_i$ and one or more references $\backslash i$. The substring matched by the reference must match the same substring that was matched by the corresponding capturing group. We focus on a subclass, which we call ordered linear rewbs where the references and capturing groups occur only outside star and union operators. Furthermore, we require that all references to a capturing group occur before the next capturing group in the rewb. In full generality, rewb matching is NP-complete, but efficient solutions exist for various subclasses. For linear rewbs with one capturing group and $k$ references, Uezato~[CPM 2026] gave an $O(k n^2 m^2)$ time and $O(n^2m^2)$ space algorithm, where $m$ is the length of the regular expression $R$ and $n$ is the length of the string $Q$. For the special case of $k=1$, Nogami and Terauchi~[MFCS 2025] gave an $O(n^2m^2)$ time and $O(n+ m^2)$ space algorithm. On the other hand, Nogami, Nakamura, and Terauchi~[arXiv 2026] gave a conditional lower bound, showing that we cannot solve the problem in $O(n^{2-ε} \mathrm{poly}(m))$ for any $ε> 0$ assuming the orthogonal vector hypothesis. Our main result is a new improved algorithm that runs in $O(n^2m+n^2k\log n)$ time and uses $O(nm)$ space, and handles the more general case of ordered linear rewbs with multiple capturing groups.

papers.title: An inverse problem on eigenfunction triple products
papers.abstract: On a connected closed smooth Riemannian manifold, the algebraic structure of the Laplace eigenfunctions, as described by eigenfunction triple products, uniquely determines the geometry. We refine this correspondence by introducing the notion of an $N$-product eigenbasis, which consists of eigenfunctions whose pairwise products may be written as linear combinations of at most $N$ basis elements. We prove that a manifold admits a $2$-product eigenbasis if and only if it is a flat torus. We also prove an analogous result for Laplace eigenvectors of bounded-degree graphs.

papers.title: On the Markov semigroup generated in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ by linear fractional divergence form operators
papers.abstract:
Let $0<s<1$ and $A$ be a constant symmetric positive definite matrix. Given the quadratic form $$ Q_A(u)=\int_{\R^N} A
abla^s u(x)\cdot 
abla^s u(x)\,dx, $$ where $
abla^s$ denotes the Riesz fractional gradient, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions such that $Q_A$ defines a Dirichlet form. In strike contrast with the local case $s=1$, positive definiteness of a constant matrix is not sufficient for the Markov property when $0<s<1$. We also describe the associated symmetric Markov semigroup and its $L^p$ realizations, prove the existence of a smooth nonnegative heat kernel and establish a bounded $H^\infty$ functional calculus.

papers.title: Spherical and lacunary maximal operators on rank one Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type
papers.abstract: The spherical maximal operator of order $μ$ was introduced by El Kohen in the setting of real hyperbolic spaces, where its $L^p$-boundedness properties were investigated. In this paper, we extend this operator to rank-one Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type and establish sufficient conditions on $μ$ for its boundedness on $L^p$, $1<p\leq\infty$. We also obtain a necessary condition for $L^p$-boundedness when $μ$ is real and $1<p<\infty$. For $1<p\leq 2$, the necessary and sufficient conditions coincide, yielding the sharp range of real $μ$ in this regime. Finally, we establish sufficient conditions for the $L^p$-boundedness of the corresponding lacunary spherical maximal operator for $1<p\leq\infty$.

papers.title: Shape effects on the Shafranov shift of Solov'ev equilibria with prescribed boundaries
papers.abstract: The Shafranov shift, the outward displacement of the magnetic axis of a toroidal plasma, is known analytically for circular and elliptical cross-sections, whereas its dependence on shape in strongly shaped plasmas has not been studied systematically. Here the shift is analyzed for a wide range of prescribed boundaries, at fixed profiles or poloidal beta, using exact Solov'ev solutions of the Grad--Shafranov equation with the boundary imposed in a least-squares sense. For shaped boundaries the shift depends on the point from which it is measured, usually the geometric center, the midpoint of the radial extent of the boundary. Therefore, a straight-cylinder equilibrium with the same plasma shape is introduced as the zero-shift reference state, and the shift is measured from its magnetic axis. With this reference, some known features of the shift measured from the geometric center turn out to be effects of the reference point, whose error depends only on the boundary and can also make the shift negative. Three boundary parametrizations are used to analyze positive and negative triangularity, squareness from square to concave shapes, and non-convex star polygons of arbitrary symmetry order. At fixed poloidal beta the shift depends only weakly on triangularity: the larger shift of negative than of positive triangularity plasmas obtained with the geometric center is an effect of the reference point and nearly disappears with the cylindrical reference. Negative squareness and concavity, instead, reduce the shift itself: for concave plasma cross-sections it is almost half that of elliptical and D-shaped ones.

papers.title: Size and shape of condensing steam jets and plumes
papers.abstract: Droplet-laden cloud dynamics emerge from coupled phase transitions and turbulent mixing. Combining experiments and mean-field theory, we establish scaling laws for steam-injected clouds in unsaturated air seeded with condensation nuclei. Depending on whether the cloud is confined to the initial momentum-dominated zone of the jet or extends into the buoyancy-dominated plume, two asymptotic regimes arise. In the momentum regime, cloud dimensions scale with the injector radius. In the buoyancy regime, size follows a $\dot{m}^{2/5}$ scaling, where $\dot{m}$ is the injected steam mass flow rate. Assuming interdroplet air remains humidity saturated, our mean-field analysis predicts cloud persistence governed by enthalpy and humidity mixing. These findings bridge microphysical processes and macroscale dynamics, offering a quantitative framework for atmospheric cloud evolution.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Uncertainty-Guided Boundary Refinement for Reliable Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Accurate biomedical image segmentation requires not only high global overlap but also reliable delineation of clinically meaningful boundaries. In blood-smear microscopy, cytoplasm and nucleus contours provide the structural basis for downstream morphology analysis; however, deep segmentation models may remain uncertain or overconfident near ambiguous boundary regions even when achieving strong Dice scores. This work proposes a Reliability-Aware Boundary Refinement Network (RABR-Net), a two-stage framework for reliability-aware biomedical image segmentation. A strong UNet++ EfficientNet-B4 base segmenter first produces initial class probabilities and logits. Predictive entropy, test-time augmentation variance, margin uncertainty, foreground probability gradients, and foreground soft-boundary cues are combined with the multiclass probabilities into a reliability-aware representation. This representation guides a gated residual refiner that selectively corrects uncertain boundary regions while preserving confident regions of the base prediction. The framework is evaluated using overlap accuracy, class-wise Dice, Boundary Dice, HD95/ASSD, expected calibration error, risk-coverage analysis, qualitative correction maps, and paired statistical testing. As a separate diagnostic analysis, we additionally characterize the sensitivity of the selected base segmenter to deterministic microscopy image perturbations.

papers.title: Reconstruction and Reflection of Positive Experiences through Resurfacing Laughter-indexed Everyday Moments
papers.abstract: Positive everyday moments often escape deliberate recording, while continuous self-tracking can generate extensive records that are difficult to revisit. We explore laughter as a naturally occurring, sparse index for constructing contextualized personal records to support later reconstruction and reflection. A formative study with 12 participants characterized laughter as an affective but semantically incomplete index and informed \textit{LaughAnchor}, a mobile and wearable self-tracking system. During participant-initiated recording, the system assembles detected laughter and aligned context into candidate moments for later reconstruction and reflection, with layered context disclosure, user-controlled curation, and near-term and long-term resurfacing. In a three-week field deployment with 12 participants, passive indexing preserved moments they considered unlikely to record deliberately but valued retrospectively. During resurfacing, participants attributed affective re-experiencing to laughter and used additional context both to reconstruct episodes and to explore already-recalled experiences. Across moments and reviews, resurfacing supported rediscovery and broader awareness of relationships, routines, and emotional states. These findings inform self-tracking designs that use sparse affective indices to organize contextual records for reconstruction and reflection, while keeping interpretation and retention under user control.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Conformal Prediction: Embedding PDE Consistency into Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification for Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Neural operators such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) achieve high accuracy in approximating solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs), but two fundamental challenges hinder deployment in safety-critical engineering: (1) a structural approximation barrier from FNO's translation equivariance that prevents learning Dirichlet boundary conditions, and (2) the lack of uncertainty bounds when multiple operators are chained in multi-physics cascades. First, we prove that FNO's translation equivariance creates a fundamental approximation barrier for PDEs with non-trivial boundary conditions (Theorem 1), and that coordinate channels resolve this (Theorem 2), validated by up to 63x error reduction across five scenarios. Second, we formalize error propagation in operator cascades: under an explicit TV-Lipschitz condition on downstream conditional mechanisms, we bound the per-stage coverage gap by the stage failure probability plus a mechanism-response term proportional to upstream prediction error (Theorem 3), and show that passing predicted fields between stages degrades coverage far more than error-matched perturbations. On a 3D electromagnetic-thermal-structural cascade, coordinate channels reduce coupling error from 18.5% to 5.0%. For per-stage UQ, we propose Physics-Informed Conformal Prediction (PI-CP), which embeds PDE residuals into the nonconformity score, complementary to recent physics-residual CP (Gopakumar et al., 2025), achieving 89-91% coverage across six physics scenarios. We further identify a boundary of diffusion-based UQ: on well-conditioned forward PDEs, the trained FNO's residual is too small for diffusion models to capture meaningful uncertainty (38-53% coverage). An industrial application, fiber-optic gyroscope bias instability prediction, validates the framework with 3.7-8.0x improvement over analytical baselines.

papers.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
papers.abstract: Spatial reasoning depends not only on metric properties such as distance, angle, and shape, but also on topological relations that remain invariant under continuous deformation. Cognitive science identifies these relations as foundational to spatial understanding, yet foundation-model evaluations largely focus on metric or viewpoint-dependent relations. We introduce MindTopo, a benchmark of topological intuition across five properties grounded in cognitive science and formal topology, namely continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots. MindTopo evaluates each property at two cognitive levels. Reasoning asks a model to identify topological relations or infer how they change. Planning instantiates a foundation model as a closed-loop agent whose policy selects environment actions. MindTopo provides a Core Set of 3,900 instances across 13 procedurally generated task types, split into an Easy and a Hard level, and an Extended Set of 11,035 original instances. On the Core Set, we benchmark 13 multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and study agent configurations augmented with image and video generation, covering seven video generative models in planning settings. Every MLLM performs better on reasoning than on planning. On the Easy level, where human scores are available, the strongest model trails humans in both reasoning and planning. On Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning improve reasoning more than planning. Generated observations retain local cues and reach solved endpoints, yet none of the 1,890 evaluated video rollouts passes all process-validity checks.

papers.title: One Precessing Jet Pair, Diverse Core-Collapse Supernova Remnant Morphologies
papers.abstract: We produce a diverse set of observed core-collapse supernova (CCSN)-type morphologies using a precessing pair of opposite jets within the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) framework. We conduct a three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulation of a precessing pair of jets that explode a massive star, and find that a single precessing pair of opposite jets can generate S-shaped structures, pipe-spout-blowout features as observed in the Cygnus Loop, multiple apparent pairs of opposite protrusions similar to some morphological features in S147, and H-shaped structures with a prominent bar, similar to the one observed in the 3C 397 remnant. At small scales, the jets form clumps and filaments, resulting from instabilities and vortices that the jets induce in the ejecta as they interact with the stellar material. We did not aim the simulation to reproduce any particular CCSN remnant, but rather to explore the resulting morphological features. Our finding of simulated features similar to observed ones supports the role of jets in exploding CCSNe and, in turn, is compatible with the claim that the JJEM might be the primary explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra when $2 \in R^\times$, costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $π\colon S \to R$ with $π(1) = 1$. In particular, the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over these fields is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ when $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. An implementation for the standard tower over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $q = p^k$ with $p \le 2^{31}-1$ an odd prime and $k \le 12$ is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface pyfastcd, available on PyPI. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method over $\mathbb{R}$, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$ for both single and batched products and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication.

papers.title: The Local Embedding Problem for Hardy Spaces of Dirichlet Series
papers.abstract: We solve the local embedding problem for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. For every $2<p<\infty$, the global $\mathscr{H}^p$-norm controls the $L^p$-norm of a Dirichlet polynomial on every unit interval of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1/2$: $\sup_{θ\in\mathbb{R}}\int_θ^{θ+1}\left|P\left(\frac12+\mathrm{i}t\right)\right|^p\mathrm{d}t\le C_p\left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathscr{H}^p}^{p}$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$, not on the interval or on the number and choice of primes occurring in $P$. The inequality was previously known at $p=2$ and, by taking powers, at every even exponent; it had been conjectured that these were the only positive cases above $2$. Together with the known counterexamples for $0<p<2$, our theorem shows that the embedding holds for finite $p$ exactly when $p\ge2$. The proof uses duality to control many critical-line evaluations together. A frequency decomposition isolates the contribution for which the relevant frequencies can nearly coincide. We estimate it by replacing the leading terms in the logarithms of the Euler factors with Gaussian variables, using the same variable for each prime at all evaluation points; the accumulated errors remain bounded. Comparison with a critical branching random walk and estimates for a finite-cyclic square function then give a bound independent of the number of prime variables. For $1\le p<\infty$, known equivalences also give the sharp range for the conformally invariant half-plane embedding, the reverse transfer of local Carleson-measure estimates, and boundedness of all characteristic-zero Gordon--Hedenmalm composition operators.

papers.title: Search for the process $e^+e^-\to f_1(1285)$ at the SND detector
papers.abstract: In the experiment with the SND detector at the VEPP-2000 $e^+e^-$ collider, a search is performed for the direct production of the $C$-even $f_1(1285)$ resonance in $e^+e^-$ collisions. The analysis is based on data with an integrated luminosity of about 200 pb$^{-1}$, accumulated in the center-of-mass energy range of 1.14--1.46 GeV, of which about 72 pb$^{-1}$ were recorded near the maximum of the $f_1(1285)$ resonance. The $f_1(1285)$ production cross section at the resonance maximum $σ(e^+e^-\to f_1)=(31\pm 13\pm 4)$ pb and the branching fraction $B(f_1(1285)\to e^+e^-)=(3.5\pm 1.4\pm 0.5)\times 10^{-9}$ have been measured. The significance of the observation of the $e^+e^-\to f_1(1285)$ process is $2.5σ$. Since the significance is low, we also present the upper limits at the 90% confidence level: $σ(e^+e^-\to f_1)<48\mbox{ pb}$ and $B(f_1(1285)\to e^+e^-)<5.4\times 10^{-9}$.

papers.title: Searching for New Physics with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Finding new physics (NP) is the fundamental problem in particle physics today. Studying anomalies, i.e., measurements of low-energy observables whose values disagree with the predictions of the Standard Model (SM), is a powerful search strategy. The SM Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general model-independent framework for parametrizing NP; given some anomalies, it is natural to try to find the SMEFT operator(s) that can explain them. This is a challenging task because (i) the number of SMEFT operators is enormous, and (ii) at loop level there are very complicated correlations among the operators. Analyses by humans typically rely on phenomenological intuition to decide which operators are relevant. This is often biased and does not explore the complete SMEFT operator space. Interestingly, reinforcement learning (RL) techniques excel at tasks that require decision making to achieve their goals. In this paper, we introduce an RL method that can be used to find the SMEFT operators that explain any anomalies. Using some explicit examples, we demonstrate that our RL method can be used to efficiently search for NP at the level of SMEFT. The RL training can be performed efficiently using standard CPU resources, without requiring specialized computing hardware.

papers.title: Total Simulated Survey Error: Designing and Diagnosing Survey Responses from Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language models (LLMs), having been trained on vast amounts of human-generated data, may encode the opinions, attitudes, and behaviors of these humans. As such, LLMs show promise in mimicking human-like patterns that facilitate their use in simulating people in a wide variety of contexts. One such context is using LLMs as 'silicon samples', i.e., proxies of people in answering survey questions to establish public opinion, design policies, or use as (social) scientific data. However, several critical questions of social biases, generalization, and technical limitations remain, further complicated by a vast design space open to simulation designers. In addition, LLM-simulated surveys often lean on existing survey infrastructure, e.g., survey questions and samples. These artifacts might not be suitable for LLMs or themselves might have errors that are then inherited by the LLM-powered survey simulations. As a result, we lack a systematic understanding of the design space of LLM-generated surveys as well as how these decisions interplay with inherent LLM limitations. In this article, we aim to systematically identify, trace, and document limitations in LLM-generated survey responses. Building on traditions in the quantitative social sciences, specifically survey methodology and measurement theory, we investigate threats to the validity of LLM-generated survey responses. To do so, we design a framework that enumerates conceptual errors and systematic biases that can occur at different stages of the survey simulation lifecycle. Our framework - called the Total Simulated Survey Error (TS2E) Framework - provides a unified and end-to-end perspective on errors in LLM-generated survey data. We illustrate the framework through a theoretical and empirical case study, which enables survey simulation designers to systematically understand, identify and reflect on errors in LLM-generated surveys.

papers.title: How an Economy Shrinks in Space: Concavity-on-Jobs and Upward Consolidation under Demographic Decline
papers.abstract: When a country's population declines, the aggregate economy appears to contract on the intensive margin: industrial diversity intact, every industry a little smaller. At the regional level, contraction is uneven and takes the extensive form: entire industries disappear, one after another. The relevant unit is the city: industries are nested by size - the hierarchy property of industrial location - each viable only above a minimum population. Necessity industries' thresholds bunch at the low end, so a city's industry count - and its jobs - is sharply concave in size (concavity on jobs). A modest loss pushes a small city below many thresholds at once; a large core sheds a few specialized industries, one at a time. Lost industries consolidate upward to the next city large enough to host them; for the worker it means a step down to a lower-paid local job if one is left, and a fall to the bottom of the hierarchy if none is. To recover the lost wage, workers move up to the apex - the only city hosting the full industry range. In Japan - two decades ahead of the OECD, Tokyo at its apex - a wage regression in real, housing-inclusive wages, on worker-level panel data for the young workers who carry the migration, finds a Tokyo-bound migration incentive that varies across origins exactly as concavity on jobs predicts.

papers.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
papers.abstract: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through an effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.

papers.title: Vishing-Tactics-Bench: Forecasting Exploitation Trajectories in Voice Phishing Calls
papers.abstract: Voice phishing (vishing) unfolds in real time; by the time a call has ended and post-hoc classification is possible, the harm has already been done. The more actionable question is which concrete harm (Information Gathering or Financial Exploitation) an ongoing call is tactically progressing toward. We present Vishing-Tactics-Bench, a benchmark grounded in Endsley's situation-awareness (SA) framework that recasts vishing defense from after-the-fact fraud classification to harm projection: predicting at each turn whether the call will reach either terminal harm. We adapt MITRE ATT&CK to vishing as a 6-tactic taxonomy (Vishing-Tactics) and label 35,340 scammer utterances across 5,645 synthetic Chinese calls. We define Exploitation Trajectory Forecasting, a survival-style protocol over the two terminal harms with three metrics: AP@k, C-index, and divergence error. Baselines ranging from a Markov heuristic to fine-tuned LLMs show that the tactical trajectory serves as an interpretable representation of the call's tactical state, supporting harm-specific forecasting, which can then be used for the downstream application of intervention selection; a stratified lead-time analysis at a tight false-alarm budget further identifies at what point in a call the trajectory signal yields early warning.

papers.title: Koszul duality for finite-dimensional Koszul algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\La$ be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual $\Ld$. Using the Koszul functors and the homological perturbation lemma, we describe the minimal projective resolution of every object of the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional graded $\La$-modules in terms of the cohomology of the corresponding complex of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules. In particular, the linear part of the minimal graded projective resolution of a finite-dimensional graded $\La$-module is a direct sum of Koszul complexes of these cohomology modules. We deduce that $\La$ is absolutely Koszul if and only if $\Ld$ is graded left co-coherent, if and only if the category of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules is abelian. As applications, we show that absolutely Koszul algebras of finite global linearity defect have finite graded finitistic dimension; we refine the graded and ungraded Koszul dualities and construct nonstandard $t$-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories. Finally, we apply these results to finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebras.

papers.title: From JPEG to CUDA Batch: Measuring RGB Input Pipeline Throughput
papers.abstract: We measure how many ready batches per second eight image input pipelines deliver to an NVIDIA L4. Each pipeline starts with RGB JPEG files and delivers synchronized CUDA float16 batches of 256 images. The benchmark contains 1314 measurements across 73 recipes. On the 34 recipes shared by all eight paths, DALI delivered a median of 19.7 batches/s and AlbumentationsX (AX) delivered 17.1. DALI was fastest on 34 of those recipes. Median peak process GPU memory was 1,872 MiB for DALI and 404 MiB for AX.

papers.title: Moments of crosscorrelation demerit factors of binary sequences
papers.abstract: Families of sequences with low mutual aperiodic crosscorrelation assist the design of systems for multi-user asynchronous communications and multiple-input multiple-output radar. The crosscorrelation demerit factor of a pair of sequences is the sum of the squared magnitudes of their crosscorrelation values at every shift when the sequences are normalized to unit Euclidean norm, and the merit factor is the reciprocal of the demerit factor. For each positive integer $\ell$, we endow the $2^{2 \ell}$ pairs of binary sequences of length $\ell$ with uniform probability measure and study the distribution of their crosscorrelation demerit factors. Sarwate showed that the mean value is always $1$ regardless of length $\ell$. We develop a method for finding an exact formula for the $p$th central moment (for any positive integer $p$) as a function of $\ell$. Formulae for the variance and third central moment ($p=2$ and $3$) are then obtained by hand calculations, while the fourth through sixth central moments are obtained by computer-assisted calculations. Our theory also shows that all the central moments must be strictly positive for $p\geq 2$ and $\ell \geq 3$.

papers.title: The Einstein Tensor from UV-regulated Field Correlations
papers.abstract: It is known that the spacetime metric can be recovered from quantum field correlators. We extend this programme by showing that the Einstein tensor can be directly written in terms of UV-regulated field correlations. The same correlation structure also directly determines the Ricci tensor, while higher coincidence derivatives recover the connection and Riemann tensor. We further show that the renormalized stress-energy tensor can be formulated within this framework, up to the standard finite renormalization freedom. These results provide a correlation-based organization of the semiclassical Einstein equations and advance the programme of formulating spacetime geometry in terms of quantum field correlations.

papers.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
papers.abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment recently reported a single event consistent with a nuclear recoil of $E_{\rm NR}\sim248$~keV in an extended-energy search. We study the accompanying inelastic-xenon channel, $χ+Xe\toχ+Xe^{*}$, as a complementary test of dark matter (DM) interpretations of such high-recoil events. Using the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework, we compute the inelastic-xenon rates for representative scenarios including accelerated DM populations and inelastic dark matter. Their signal patterns in the S1--S2 plane are reconstructed. The nuclear de-excitation shifts these signals toward the electronic-recoil band, where they may overlap with clustered isotope backgrounds. We then propose a schematic, physics-motivated background model to estimate their detectability. For many benchmarks, the inelastic-xenon rates are $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ of the elastic rates or below, and the projected sensitivity remains weak even at $200~{\rm tonne\,yr}$ for the scenarios investigated. Our results provide additional inelastic-xenon signal predictions for various DM scenarios and motivate improved high-energy background modeling and detector calibration for future searches.

papers.title: Carbon-aware Resource Management for Latency-Sensitive Cloud Computing Environments: A Taxonomy and Future Directions
papers.abstract: The proliferation of cloud-based latency-sensitive workloads, such as autonomous driving, real-time healthcare services, industrial automation, immersive interactive services, and intelligent AI-based applications requires infrastructures tuned to meet stringent latency constraints. Today, these workloads are reshaping the cloud from a general-purpose computing platform into a diverse ecosystem of workload-specific cloud environments. As demand for latency-sensitive workloads grows, cloud providers must scale their infrastructures accordingly, adversely increasing the carbon footprint and challenging net-zero goals. However, the strict performance requirements and rigid deployment patterns used to satisfy latency Service Level Objectives (SLOs) constrains conventional carbon optimization. Therefore, novel carbon-aware techniques are needed to exploit application-specific opportunities for reducing both operational and embodied carbon footprints while preserving latency guarantees. This survey examines carbon-aware resource management for latency-sensitive cloud computing environments. We introduce a holistic taxonomy that organizes existing techniques by carbon management objective, workload management mechanism, control architecture, system tier, latency requirements, and deployment stage. Then, we use this taxonomy to classify and critically analyze existing approaches, revealing the interactions and trade-offs between latency guarantees and operational and embodied carbon reduction. Finally, we identify limitations in the literature and present a structured research agenda for the design of sustainable latency-sensitive cloud systems.

papers.title: Spin-current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in $p$-wave antialtermagnets
papers.abstract: We show that $p$-wave magnetic insulators efficiently generate magnetization via a linear thermal magnon Edelstein effect. Furthermore, they can generate perfectly nonreciprocal spin currents through a purely even-order nonlinear response. This makes them promising candidates for spin-current rectification. More generally, we find that odd-parity-wave magnets with coplanar ground states host magnons with zero magnetic moment in the plane. Instead the magnons carry a colinear, out-of-plane magnetic moment, placing coplanar odd-parity-wave magnets within the class of antialtermagnets. We establish these general results using symmetry arguments and demonstrate them explicitly for a two-dimensional model with a coplanar ground state containing the minimal number of sublattices, inspired by the ground state of CeNiAsO. Our conclusions hold both in the absence and in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.

papers.title: Efficient All-in-One Weather Restoration using Spectral Harmonization
papers.abstract: Adverse weather conditions such as rain, haze, and snow significantly degrade image quality, posing challenges for both human perception and physical AI. Existing restoration methods require large computational budgets, struggling to process high-resolution images and handle different degradations. In this paper, we present Frequency Reconstruction via Spectral Harmonization, a novel lightweight all-in-one restoration method that explicitly decomposes feature representations into high- and low-frequency components at each scale of a hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture. By combining spectral decomposition with spatial processing through Fourier-based skip connections, FReSH-IR captures complementary frequency information without sacrificing spatial detail. Our approach achieves similar restoration quality with 80% fewer parameters and operations than transformer-based models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method offers a great efficiency-performance trade-off, highlighting its practical applications in constrained-resource systems.

papers.title: HINT: Human-Intent Inception for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Humans can perform complex manipulations given a simple intent through an overall instruction, while continuously adapting to evolving visual observations. However, current vision-language action (VLA) models and other action policies struggle to realize this high-level intelligent behavior under dense, evolving visual inputs and sparse language guidance. Visual correlations can then dominate semantic intent, leading actions to follow visual shortcuts rather than human goals. We present HINT (Human-INTent INcepTion), an agentic framework inspired by the human manipulation principles: semantic intent changes sparsely at manipulation-pattern transitions, whereas continuous control primarily depends on the evolving object-hand relationship. HINT invokes semantic reasoning only at pattern transitions to resolve the current subtask and target, then maintains this commitment through multi-view grounding and visual tracking. We explore two visual interfaces-image-space semantic highlighting and attention-prior injection-to communicate the tracked intent to the action policy without introducing additional trainable parameters into the foundation action model. Experiments across three long-horizon tasks and out-of-distribution variants show that HINT substantially improves intent understanding, task progress, and end-to-end success across two foundation policies while preserving low-latency control. Project page: https://robot-hint.github.io/

papers.title: ViSAR: Training-Free Adaptive-$k$ Retrieval for Document Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) often leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), where late-interaction encoders are commonly used to identify document pages relevant to a user query, before answer generation by a Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM). Existing approaches typically retrieve a fixed top-$k$ number of pages regardless of query complexity, which increases LVLM latency and may degrade answer accuracy when fewer pages would be enough. We introduce ViSAR (Visual Semantic Activation Retrieval), a training-free, budget-aware adaptive-$k$ retrieval method for late-interaction visual document retrieval. ViSAR operates directly in the embedding space to construct a query-conditioned page-level similarity matrix that highlights query-relevant semantics and dynamically determines the number of pages to retrieve, within a given page budget. We evaluate our method across multiple datasets, encoders, and LVLMs. ViSAR retrieves compact, query-adapted page sets that reduce end-to-end RAG latency by up to 58.9\%, with no statistically significant accuracy loss and significant gains in several settings, compared with fixed top-$k$ and adaptive retrieval heuristics. Furthermore, we show that the similarity matrix structure correlates with answer accuracy, suggesting future directions for retrieval quality-aware document understanding.

papers.title: Late-time dark energy dynamics in $f(Q)$ gravity: A data-driven analysis
papers.abstract: The increasing precision and complementarity of late-time cosmological observations provide new opportunities to test modified gravity against the observed expansion history of the universe. The combination of DESI DR2 BAO measurements with cosmic chronometers (CC) and independent Type Ia supernova compilations provides a data-driven test of cosmic acceleration. Motivated by this progress, we investigate late-time dark energy dynamics in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity by adopting the power-law form $f(Q)=βQ^{m+1}$ and characterizing cosmic evolution through the effective equation of state (EoS) parameter. The model is constrained using CC, DESI DR2 BAO and three independent Type Ia supernova compilations, namely Pantheon+, DES-Dovekie and Union3. The inferred Hubble constant values are mutually consistent, yielding $H_0=68.0^{+2.7}_{-3.3}$, $68.2^{+2.7}_{-3.3}$ and $67.4^{+2.7}_{-3.3}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Statistically, the proposed $f(Q)$ model yields lower $χ^2_{\min}$ values and is favored by the AIC for all dataset combinations, whereas the BIC favors $Λ$CDM for the CC + DESI DR2 + Pantheon+ and CC + DESI DR2 + DES-Dovekie combinations and indicates no meaningful preference between the two models for the CC + DESI DR2 + Union3 dataset combinations. The reconstructed effective EoS characterizes the evolution of the cosmic fluid, while the deceleration parameter indicates the current accelerated expansion of the universe. Higher-order cosmographic parameters and the Statefinder and $Om(z)$ diagnostics provide complementary insights into the evolution of the cosmic expansion, while the Statefinder trajectories approach the $Λ$CDM fixed point in the far future. Overall, the power-law $f(Q)$ model provides a competitive description of the late-time expansion history and the observed cosmic acceleration.

papers.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
papers.abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

papers.title: Relative Fourier--Mukai theory for algebraic spaces
papers.abstract: We study the variation of Fourier--Mukai equivalences in proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. For bounded pseudocoherent kernels, we prove that the equivalence locus is open and commutes with arbitrary Noetherian base change. To do so, we develop a theory of relative perfectness and relative quasi-perfectness for algebraic spaces. This includes a fiberwise criteria for integral transforms with nonperfect kernels. As an application, we construct an explicit autoequivalence for elliptic fibrations.

papers.title: iPINN for Broadband CARS Phase Retrieval: A Framework for Function Approximation and Inverse Modeling Problems in Nonlinear Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (BCARS) records chemically specific vibrational spectra, but the measured signal mixes the resonant, Raman-like response of the sample with a non-resonant background that changes from one measurement to the next. Recovering the resonant response, known as phase retrieval, is an ill-posed inverse problem. We present iPINN, an inverse physics-informed neural network that predicts the positions, amplitudes, and widths of Lorentzian vibrational bands directly from a BCARS spectrum. A transformer network estimates these band parameters, and a differentiable analytical model of the resonant susceptibility rebuilds the Raman-like spectrum from them as a sum of physically defined bands. We train the network on simulated spectra in which the bands of each reference compound stay fixed while the shape and strength of the background and the noise vary. Training also encourages similar band predictions for the same compound across these variations. On a public benchmark of toluene and dimethyl sulfoxide spectra, the network reached a mean absolute error about one third of that of the best of five deep-learning baselines. Its error for dimethyl sulfoxide stayed nearly constant across three noise levels. We also used 28 spectra of seven solvents, recorded at four focal depths with different background strengths. For five of the seven solvents, the mean absolute error changed little with depth, while it varied more for the other two. These results indicate that this approach keeps phase retrieval stable for most of the tested solvents when the background changes.

papers.title: REVISE: Validity-Guided Recovery for Online Revisions in Agent Workflows
papers.abstract: Agent revisions expose a fundamental correctness--efficiency trade-off during concurrent execution. Discarding ongoing work preserves latest-version correctness but wastes progress that may remain valid, whereas reusing prior work preserves efficiency but risks propagating stale state into outputs and tool effects. Existing recovery strategies resolve this trade-off in an imbalanced way with coarse-grained policies: they either favor efficiency by allowing potentially stale work to continue, or favor correctness by restarting the workflow or recomputing a linear suffix from the earliest conflict, thereby discarding unaffected progress. We present \textsc{Revise}, a validity-guided runtime for fine-grained recovery in structured agent workflows. When a revision arrives, \textsc{Revise} first intersects its delta with recorded data and control dependencies and propagates the resulting impact through the partially executed DAG to identify affected work. It then stops invalid work, preserves validity-established progress beyond the earliest conflict, and recomputes only the affected region. Incomplete provenance conservatively expands recovery, while reused results are revalidated before commit. Analysis of real coding-agent traces show online recovery opportunities: 118 sessions retain observable work before a queued later message is delivered; across 167 overlapping assistant responses, enqueue-to-completion overlap reaches 56.55~s at p95. Across 300 challenging revision/commit executions, \textsc{Revise} matches a latest-version oracle with no stale outputs or effects. On unmodified LangGraph and LLMCompiler applications using Qwen3-14B, it reduces model calls by 40.6--56.0\% relative to full restart and by 31.3--43.6\% relative to suffix recomputation. Under serving pressure, it further reduces revision-to-correct-completion tokens by 13.26\% and improves SLO goodput by 3.07--5.43\%.

papers.title: Operator-valued maximal $f$-divergences for completely positive maps
papers.abstract: We introduce an operator-valued maximal $f$-divergence for completely positive (CP) maps between von Neumann algebras, associated with an operator convex function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. The construction takes values in the extended lower-semibounded self-adjoint part of the codomain von Neumann algebra. We prove independence of the common CP upper bound used in its computation, joint subadditivity, monotonicity under unital precomposition and normal postcomposition, a martingale convergence theorem for normal CP maps, and joint lower semicontinuity in the point-$σ$-weak topology. For normal positive functionals, our construction recovers Hiai's maximal $f$-divergence. As a consequence, we establish its joint weak lower semicontinuity for arbitrary von Neumann algebras, answering a question left open by Hiai. For $η(t)=t log t$, we obtain an operator-valued Belavkin--Staszewski (BS) relative entropy. Moreover, for normal channels with $σ$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence. Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.

papers.title: Functional Degeneracy in Neural Networks: Measurement and Pruning
papers.abstract: A central question in modern machine learning is how much a trained model can be compressed without changing its behavior, to reduce the memory, compute and energy required to deploy it. To study this, we quantify functional degeneracy through the behavioral recovery rank, the number of leading behavioral-Hessian eigendirections required to recover a model's performance to a given tolerance. Using it as a geometric benchmark for compression, we find that the rank flattens once the task is saturated, while the number of parameters retained by one-shot pruning keeps growing. This gap suggests that functional degeneracy is distributed across parameter directions and not exposed by individual weights or neurons.

papers.title: Hi-Q: Hierarchical Evidence-guided Query Refinement for Multi-Hop Question Answering
papers.abstract: A central bottleneck in multi-hop Question Answering (QA) is that the granularity at which a question is expressed often differs from the granularity at which corpus evidence is retrievable. Existing methods address this mismatch by imposing fixed graph structures over the corpus, by iteratively reformulating the query, or by executing a generated program over it, but these strategies do not explicitly decide when a query unit is already supported by evidence and when it should be refined. We formulate this bottleneck as retrievable granularity discovery and introduce Hi-Q, an evidence-conditioned framework for hierarchical query refinement. At each query node, a resolution operator tests whether retrieved evidence supports the current query unit; resolved nodes terminate, while unresolved nodes are expanded by a dependency-preserving binary operator and checked by a semantic coverage verifier. Hi-Q therefore grows a query tree whose topology is determined by corpus support signals rather than by a fixed decomposition template or a pre-built graph. We evaluate Hi-Q on three multi-hop QA benchmarks, primarily under full-corpus retrieval, where dependent evidence must be located among open-domain distractors rather than within a small annotated pool. In this setting Hi-Q reaches 52.3 EM and 64.0 F1 averaged over the three benchmarks, ahead of the iterative retrieval baseline IRCoT by 15.1 EM / 18.2 F1 on that same average, and ahead of the graph-based RAG baseline PropRAG by 11.5 EM / 12.0 F1 on MuSiQue-full, without corpus-wide graph construction. In the restricted supporting/distractor setting used by prior work, Hi-Q likewise attains the best accuracy, with 57.9 EM and 69.3 F1 on average, ahead of PropRAG by 5.6 EM / 3.9 F1 and IRCoT by 13.7 EM / 15.8 F1. The project page is available at https://hi-q-project.github.io/.

papers.title: A Chvátal--Erdős type condition for supereulerian digraphs with $α_{2}=4$
papers.abstract: A digraph is \textbf{supereulerian} if it contains a spanning closed trail. Let $α_2(D)$ denote the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing no 2-cycle. In this paper, we study the supereulerianity of digraphs with arc-strong connectivity at least 2. We identify a family $\mathcal H$ of nonsupereulerian 2-arc-strong digraphs and prove that every 2-arc-strong digraph $D$ with $α_2(D)\leq 4$ is supereulerian if and only if $D\notin\mathcal H$. In particular, every digraph $D$ satisfying $α_2(D) \le 4$ and $λ(D) \ge 3$ is supereulerian.

papers.title: Density-gradient effect in high-harmonic generation in gases
papers.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gaseous targets is the most widespread method to produce coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulses with sub-femtosecond duration. However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light--matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale imaging of biological and industrial samples, or in nonlinear optics in the XUV regime.

papers.title: LEON: Operator-Structured Latent Evolution for World Modeling
papers.abstract: Modeling action-conditioned physical evolution is fundamental to latent world models. World Action Models (WAMs) couple such models with policy learning through predictive supervision or future-conditioned action generation. Yet their latent transitions typically rely on transformer-based predictors, leaving dynamical structure to be learned implicitly from data. We derive a latent-transition formulation from controlled mechanical evolution. A common finite-dimensional projection of observable dynamics yields a shared operator family affine in physical control and an explicit projection residual. Guided by this principle, we introduce the Latent Evolution Operator Network (LEON), which adapts pretrained visual features into learned observables and evolves them through an affine family of shared operator matrices and complementary additive updates. Coefficients inferred from evolving observables and action-related context modulate the operators. We instantiate LEON in two WAM architectures while preserving their distinct original prediction targets and policy interfaces. Across single-arm and bimanual manipulation, LEON improves average policy success over corresponding WAM baselines, including under diverse perturbations. Ablations support its observable adaptation and operator-structured evolution, while controlled-system evaluations demonstrate improved extrapolation beyond training conditions.

papers.title: On the weak Lefschetz property of Artinian Gorenstein algebras of codimension three in arbitrary characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf k$ be a field, $S=\mathsf k[x,y,z]$, and $R=S/I$ be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein $\mathsf k$-algebra of codimension three. The $h$-vector of such an algebra is known to be symmetric and unimodal. Miró-Roig proved that if $\mathsf k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero and the $h$-vector of $R$ has at least three peaks, then $R$ has the weak Lefschetz property. We first observe that this statement holds over any infinite field of arbitrary characteristic, and that it follows from a theorem of Iarrobino--Kanev by an argument which is already used in special cases in the literature. We then give a second, characteristic-free proof, following the strategy of Migliore--Zanello, which is elementary and does not use the theorem of Iarrobino--Kanev, and hence does not use the Buchsbaum--Eisenbud structure theorem.

papers.title: Contact-Aided Factor-Graph Localization for Underwater Sampling
papers.abstract: Accurate state estimation for autonomous underwater vehicles performing close-range seafloor sampling remains challenging. In low-altitude operation, down-looking cameras over featureless planar seabeds produce scale ambiguity, lateral degeneracy, and inconsistent feature tracking. Meanwhile, inertial-Doppler Velocity Log (DVL) fusion alone provides no mechanism for structural drift correction. We propose a Contact-Aided Factor-Graph Localization framework that treats physical interaction as an informative geometric constraint within a smoothing-based localization formulation. The method tightly fuses suction-based manipulator contact events with adaptive visual odometry, learned object detections, and on-board sensors. Visual odometry relative-pose factors and landmark bearing-range factors are uncertainty-scaled according to inlier statistics to prevent visually weak frames from destabilizing the estimator, while contact events are modeled as high-confidence factors that induce implicit loop closures without appearance-based place recognition. Furthermore, the system can fully initialize online during motion.
