Beyond aggregate accuracy, our analysis surfaces four findings that distinguish hardware from software code completion: \emph{(i)}~performance varies sharply across HDLs, with high-level synthesis (HLS) easiest and VHDL hardest in most settings across functional pass rate, exact match (EM), and edit similarity (ES); \emph{(ii)}~hardware accuracy is non-monotonic in code-structure depth, in contrast with the monotonic depth--accuracy curve known for software; \emph{(iii)}~accuracy plateaus once the input context exceeds 2{,}048 tokens, while software completion continues to benefit from longer context; and \emph{(iv)}~certain repository-level retrievers tuned on software underperform a no-retrieval baseline on HDL repositories because their structural and dependency assumptions are violated by hardware code.

papers.title: Full-Time-Scale Power Management for Hybrid AC/DC/DS Microgrid with Dynamic Concatenation and Global Equivalent Circuit Modeling
papers.abstract: Hybrid AC/DC/distributed energy storage (DS) microgrids (MGs) provide an effective solution for improving power accessibility and supply reliability in remote and isolated areas.Conventional static power management aims to proportionally allocate power based on unit ratings by scheduling the operation of interlinking converters (ILCs). Recent studies on transient power management emphasize inertia coupling among subgrids by dynamically regulating ILC power flows, thereby enhancing the system resilience against disturbances. In existing literature, these two objectives are normally addressed in a separate fashion and a unified scheme to simultaneously achieve them is rarely found. Furthermore, conventional static management neglects droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations which may seriously compromise the safe operation of sensitive loads. To address these limitations, in this paper, we proposes a full-timescale (FTS) power management for the hybrid MG is proposed.Autonomous frequency/voltage restoration controls are deployed in each subgrid to eliminate droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations, based on which a novel FTS dynamic concatenator is proposed to chain up the static power sharing and transient inertia sharing across different timescales. Moreover, a novel global equivalent circuit model (GECM) is presented to interpret the holistic hybrid system from electrical circuit perspective. Then the static and transient performance of the complex hybrid AC/DC/DS MG can be quantitatively characterized to facilitate easier engineering practices. In-house experiments validate that the proposed FTS dynamic concatenator ensures static power sharing and transient inertia sharing through the ILC in full timescales.

papers.title: A choice-based axiomatization of Nash equilibrium
papers.abstract: An axiomatization of Nash equilibrium is provided for games of complete information in normal form. The Nash equilibrium correspondence is shown to be the unique solution concept that satisfies four simple and intuitive axioms. Two axioms reflect a mild form of individual rationality: one states that any profile of dominant strategies in a game must be a solution, whereas the other says that any solution to a game should not depend on strictly dominated strategies. The remaining two axioms are adaptations to non-cooperative games of standard choice-theoretic axioms about contraction and expansion consistency.

papers.title: A General Theorem for Non-Simultaneous Hat Guessing Puzzles
papers.abstract: The prisoners and hats puzzle, or simply the hat puzzle, is a family of games in which a group of prisoners are each assigned a colored hat and are asked to guess the color of their own hat. Various versions of the puzzle arise depending on the number of prisoners, the number of possible hat colors, and the information available to them before and after the game begins. These puzzles are broadly classified according to whether the prisoners' declarations are made simultaneously or non-simultaneously. In this paper we present a general theorem concerning the existence of a winning strategy when the declarations are non-simultaneous. We also discuss the relationship between the construction of such strategies and the Axiom of Choice, as well as their connection to the simultaneous-declaration case.

papers.title: Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. For the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with an edge we have both plane-wave solutions describing bulk states and exponentially localized solutions that correspond to edge modes. The analytic bulk-edge connection is employed to identify the conditions under which the edge states emerge from the bulk spectrum. The pseudospin ordering rotates under the energy change of the edge modes but is energy-independent for the bulk modes, except for the opposite sign in the upper and the lower band. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.

papers.title: Influence of Network Topology and Vaccination Strategies on HPV Dynamics: A Simulation Study Using the SeCoNet Growth Model
papers.abstract: This study examines how contact network topology influences the effectiveness of vaccination programs in the context of human papillomavirus (HPV) transmission. Using the SeCoNet sexual contact network growth model, we evaluate age based, ring based, and several centrality based vaccination strategies across the overall, male, and female cohorts, focusing on peak incidence, timing of peak prevalence, and cumulative incidence. The simulations show that degree, betweenness, and percolation centrality based strategies are generally the most effective, while ring vaccination achieves the greatest reduction in cumulative incidence among females. Network topology also plays a critical role: higher average degree reduces vaccination effectiveness, whereas higher power-law exponent, longer average shortest path length, and stronger clustering improve vaccination outcomes. The results highlight the importance of incorporating network structure into the design of HPV vaccination programs.

papers.title: Controllable Generative Trajectory Prediction via Weak Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: Deep generative models such as conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) have shown great promise for predicting trajectories of surrounding agents in autonomous vehicle planning. State-of-the-art models have achieved remarkable accuracy in such prediction tasks. Besides accuracy, diversity is also crucial for safe planning because human behaviors are inherently uncertain and multimodal. However, existing methods generally lack a scheme to generate controllably diverse trajectories, which is arguably more useful than randomly diversified trajectories, to the end of safe planning. To address this, we propose PrefCVAE, an augmented CVAE framework that uses weakly labeled preference pairs to imbue latent variables with semantic attributes. Using average velocity as an example attribute, we demonstrate that PrefCVAE enables controllable, semantically meaningful predictions without degrading baseline accuracy. Our results show the effectiveness of preference supervision as a cost-effective way to enhance sampling-based generative models.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
papers.abstract: Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $ν\neqκ$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally. Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.

papers.title: Two stage GNSS outlier detection for factor graph optimization based GNSS-RTK/INS/odometer fusion
papers.abstract: GNSS pseudorange outliers severely disturb carrier-phase ambiguity resolution and positioning, particularly during signal blockages and recovery. Temporal Doppler consistency provides a reliable short-term range-change reference, but requires valid measurements at both endpoints and becomes unavailable upon signal re-acquisition. This paper presents a two-stage pseudorange screening framework that complements Doppler consistency with joint IMU-odometer motion prediction. The second stage compares predicted and measured temporal changes of double-differenced pseudoranges against an accepted anchor epoch without using current GNSS observations in the motion reference. A first-order error model separates anchor, relative-motion, and measurement uncertainties to propagate factor-graph covariance into the chi-square detection gate, and both stages adjust code weights through a closed-form minimum-inflation rule. Under continuous tracking, Doppler screening reduces RTK 3D RMSE by 96.18% and outperforms the a-contrario baseline by 58.56%. When Doppler checks are unavailable, joint IMU-odometer prediction detects a 10-m outlier change in 99.58% of trials after 30 s and 73.72% after 60 s, reducing RIO 3D RMSE by up to 78.51% after outages while RI screening outperforms an inertial-aided baseline by 70.42% in simulation and 39.11% in deep urban canyons.

papers.title: UniSage: A Unified and Diagnosis-Driven Sampling Framework for Microservice Systems
papers.abstract: Traces and logs are essential observability signals for diagnosing microservice failures, but their massive volume makes full retention prohibitively expensive. Sampling is therefore widely used to reduce storage and analysis overhead. However, existing sampling frameworks suffer from two key limitations. First, they typically follow a sample-before-analysis paradigm, where data is discarded before its diagnostic value is known, risking the loss of critical evidence for downstream analysis. Second, they mainly focus on trace sampling, while logs are either compressed or filtered independently, which can break the contextual linkage between anomalous traces and their explanatory log messages. To address these limitations, we propose UniSage, a unified and diagnosis-driven sampling framework for microservice systems. UniSage is unified in two senses: it integrates lightweight analysis into the sampling pipeline to guide retention decisions, and it jointly samples traces and logs by exploiting their cross-modal correlations. Evaluations on three multi-modal microservice datasets show that UniSage consistently preserves more diagnostic evidence under tight budgets. At the 5% budget, UniSage improves average diagnostic trace recall by 6.8%-22.0% over existing trace sampling baselines and achieves the highest diagnostic log recall on the evaluated log-labeled datasets. UniSage also remains practical, with runtime measurements showing modest overhead across the evaluated workloads.

papers.title: Membership Inference Attacks on Recommender System: A Survey
papers.abstract: Recommender systems (RecSys) have been widely applied across e-commerce, finance, healthcare, and social media and have become increasingly influential in shaping user behavior and decision-making, underscoring their growing impact across domains. Since RecSys heavily relies on user data, its privacy concerns are significant and need to be addressed urgently. Recent studies on membership inference attacks (MIAs) in RecSys highlight this need. MIAs aim to infer whether a user or an interaction record was used to train a target RecSys model. Successful MIAs can lead to severe privacy breaches, such as revealing sensitive aspects of users' lifestyles. MIAs in RecSys have features distinct from those targeting classification models or large language models. However, no systematic survey on this topic has yet been conducted. We present the first comprehensive survey on RecSys MIAs, exploring their taxonomy, design principles, evaluation methods, and defense mechanisms. Based on the summary of existing studies in this area, we also outline several promising future research directions. This survey aims to raise awareness of privacy risks among RecSys researchers, practitioners, and users, and promote privacy protection practices in RecSys design.

papers.title: ReST-RL: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning through Unified Self-Training and Value-Guided Search
papers.abstract: With respect to improving the reasoning accuracy of LLMs, the representative reinforcement learning (RL) method - Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) - has achieved critical success, yet it still suffers from the issue of insignificant reward signals. This paper introduces ReST-RL, a unified Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) policy-value framework that reconnects policy optimization and value-guided search to improve LLM reasoning ability. Firstly, ReST-GRPO adopts an optimized ReST-style algorithm to reshape the policy-induced trajectory distribution by increasing the reward variance of GRPO sampling and exposing the policy to more informative partial states, thereby improving training efficiency and effectiveness. Then, we further introduce a decoding optimization method, VM-MCTS, which trains a Value Model (VM) from self-collected Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) targets and deploys it through an adapted MCTS algorithm to provide precise process signals and verification scores, further enhancing reasoning accuracy. These two stages are internally dependent - ReST-GRPO yields higher quality trajectories for value learning with VM-MCTS, which in turn enables more effective inference-time search. We validate our framework on multiple coding benchmarks (e.g., APPS, BigCodeBench, and HumanEval), where it significantly outperforms other reinforcement training baselines (naive GRPO, DAPO, and ReST-DPO), as well as decoding and verification baselines (e.g., PRM-BoN and ORM-MCTS), indicating its power to strengthen LLM reasoning capability. Moreover, we further evaluate ReST-RL on out-of-domain math and science reasoning tasks, where it achieves improved performance without target-domain tuning and favorable end-to-end efficiency trade-offs, providing preliminary transfer evidence beyond our primary coding domain.

papers.title: Symbolic Branch Networks: Tree-Inherited Neural Models for Interpretable Multiclass Classification
papers.abstract: Symbolic Branch Networks (SBNs) are neural models whose architecture is derived directly from an ensemble of decision trees. Each root-to-parent-of-leaf decision path is mapped to a hidden neuron, while the matrices W1 (feature-to-branch) and W2 (branch-to-class) encode the structural relationships induced by the teacher ensemble. This provides an explicit correspondence between teacher branches and neural components, enabling feature-level and branch-level interpretation while retaining the flexibility of gradient-based optimization. The primary configuration studied in this work trains the teacher-derived feature-to-branch matrix W1 through gradient-based learning while keeping the branch-to-class matrix W2 fixed; this configuration is denoted SBN1,0. Across 29 multiclass tabular datasets, this configuration improves upon the teacher ensemble on 28 of 29 datasets, increasing mean accuracy from 84.0% to 87.9%. For reference, XGBoost and TabPFN achieve mean accuracies of 87.3% and 91.3%, respectively, on the same datasets. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on dataset-level mean accuracies indicates a statistically significant improvement of SBN1,0 over the teacher ensemble (p=4.71x10-7). Beyond predictive performance, SBN provides an explicit structural basis for interpretation. Global feature importance can be derived from the teacher-induced feature-to-branch connectivity, while individual predictions can be traced to selected branch-neurons, their associated features, and their class contributions. An analysis across ten independently constructed teacher ensembles shows consistent predictions for a selected instance but only partial stability in its local feature rankings.

papers.title: EDGChain-E: A Decentralized Git-Based Framework for Versioning Encrypted Energy Data
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new decentralized framework, named EDGChain-E (Encrypted-Data-Git Chain for Energy), designed to manage version-controlled, encrypted energy data using blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System. The framework incorporates a Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) to orchestrate collaborative data governance across the lifecycle of energy research and operations, such as smart grid monitoring, demand forecasting, and peer-to-peer energy trading. In EDGChain-E, initial commits capture the full encrypted datasets-such as smart meter readings or grid telemetry-while subsequent updates are tracked as encrypted Git patches, ensuring integrity, traceability, and privacy. This versioning mechanism supports secure collaboration across multiple stakeholders (e.g., utilities, researchers, regulators) without compromising sensitive or regulated information. We highlight the framework's capability to maintain FAIR-compliant (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) provenance of encrypted data. By embedding hash-based content identifiers in Merkle trees, the system enables transparent, auditable, and immutable tracking of data changes, thereby supporting reproducibility and trust in decentralized energy applications.

papers.title: BitBypass: A New Direction in Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models with Bitstream Camouflage
papers.abstract: The inherent risk of generating harmful and unsafe content by Large Language Models (LLMs), has highlighted the need for their safety alignment. Various techniques like supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and red-teaming were developed for ensuring the safety alignment of LLMs. However, the robustness of these aligned LLMs is always challenged by adversarial attacks that exploit unexplored and underlying vulnerabilities of the safety alignment. In this paper, we develop a novel black-box jailbreak attack, called BitBypass, that leverages hyphen-separated bitstream camouflage for jailbreaking aligned LLMs. This represents a new direction in jailbreaking by exploiting fundamental information representation of data as continuous bits, rather than leveraging prompt engineering or adversarial manipulations. Our evaluation of five state-of-the-art LLMs, namely GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Claude 3.5, Llama 3.1, and Mixtral, in adversarial perspective, revealed the capabilities of BitBypass in bypassing their safety alignment and tricking them into generating harmful and unsafe content. Further, we observed that BitBypass outperforms several state-of-the-art jailbreak attacks in terms of stealthiness and attack success. Overall, these results highlights the effectiveness and efficiency of BitBypass in jailbreaking these state-of-the-art LLMs.

papers.title: LiteLMGuard: Seamless and Lightweight On-Device Guardrails for Small Language Models against Quantization Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: The growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has influenced the development of Small Language Models (SLMs) for on-device deployment across smartphones and edge devices, offering enhanced privacy, reduced latency, server-free functionality, and improved user experience. However, due to on-device resource constraints, SLMs undergo size optimization through compression techniques like quantization, which inadvertently introduce fairness, ethical and privacy risks. Critically, quantized SLMs may respond to harmful queries directly, without requiring adversarial manipulation, raising significant safety and trust concerns. To address this, we propose LiteLMGuard, an on-device guardrail that provides real-time, prompt-level defense for quantized SLMs. Additionally, our guardrail is designed to be model-agnostic such that it can be seamlessly integrated with any SLM, operating independently of underlying architectures. Our LiteLMGuard formalizes deep learning (DL)-based prompt filtering by leveraging semantic understanding to classify prompt answerability for SLMs. Built on our curated Answerable-or-Not dataset, LiteLMGuard employs ELECTRA as the candidate model with 97.75% answerability classification accuracy. The on-device deployment of LiteLMGuard enabled real-time offline filtering with over 85% defense-rate against harmful prompts (including jailbreak attacks), 94% filtering accuracy and ~135 ms average latency. These results demonstrate LiteLMGuard as a lightweight robust defense mechanism for effectively and efficiently securing on-device SLMs against Open Knowledge Attacks.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Techniques for Distributed Entanglement Generation and Purification
papers.abstract: We develop a purification-aware optimization framework for distributing high-fidelity entangled states over quantum networks. In repeater-based architectures, the framework jointly selects entanglement swapping, fusion or graph-state growth, and purification operations to maximize generation rate under a fidelity threshold. Different purification models can be incorporated through their fidelity-update, success-probability, and latency rules. We introduce purification-augmented generation trees and dynamic programming (DP) algorithms for entangled-pair (EP) distribution. Hypergraph-flow linear programming (LP) formulations support level-based structures and concurrent generation across multiple trees and demands. We extend the framework to GHZ states and arbitrary graph states constructed from remote EP resources, introduce graph-state construction primitives, and derive closed-form fidelity-vector updates for GHZ fusion and purification and graph-state growth and purification. We provide optimal formulations under the adopted models, discretization, and purification bounds, together with efficient DP and LP heuristics. We bound fidelity- and rate-discretization errors and establish convergence for fixed constructions under stated regularity conditions. NetSquid simulations of EP generation using our LP approach show an average 160% increase in generation rate over the compared prior approaches, with gains up to 330% in some scenarios. GHZ and graph-state simulations demonstrate the heuristics' effectiveness in balancing generation rate, output fidelity, and computational overhead.

papers.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $ψ$-Fueter operator
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.

papers.title: The infinitesimal subgroup of interpretable groups in some dp-minimal valued fields
papers.abstract: We continue our local analysis of groups interpretable in various dp-minimal valued fields, as introduced in [8]. We associate with every infinite group $G$ interpretable in those fields an infinite type-definable infinitesimal subgroup $ν(G)$, generated by the four infinitesimal subgroups $ν_D(G)$ associated with the distinguished sorts $K$, $\textbf{k}$, $Γ$ and $K/\mathcal{O}$. To show that $ν(G)$ is type-definable, we show that the resulting subgroups $ν_D(G)$ commute with each other as $D$ ranges over the four distinguished sorts. We then study the basic properties of $ν(G)$. Among others, we show that $ν(G_1\times G_2)=ν(G_1)\times ν(G_2)$ and that if $G_1\le G$ is a definable subgroup then $ν(G_1)$ is relatively definable in $ν(G)$. We also discuss possible connections between $\mathrm{dp\text{-}rk}(ν(G))$ and elimination of imaginaries.

papers.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
papers.abstract: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.

papers.title: Finding pure Nash equilibria in large random games
papers.abstract: Best Response Dynamics (BRD) constitute a family of strategy update rules designed to identify Pure Nash Equilibria (PNEs) in strategic games. In each iteration, a player is selected uniformly at random and adopts a best response strategy, maximising their payoff given the current strategies of the other players. If no improvement is possible for the selected player, another is chosen. The process terminates upon reaching a state where no player wishes to deviate, corresponding to a PNE. However, convergence is not guaranteed as either PNEs may not exist, or the dynamics may become confined within substructures of the game, which we call traps, that admit no PNEs. We investigate this behaviour in the context of random games with $N$ players, each choosing between two actions and receiving independently and identically distributed payoffs. The payoff distribution is permitted to have atoms, allowing for the possibility of ties. The induced dynamics define a class of random walks on the $N$-dimensional hypercube, where the landscape includes two types of absorbing sets: PNEs and traps. Our analysis encompasses BRD, simple random walks, and a broad class of nearest-neighbour processes. We prove that, with high probability, these dynamics reach a PNE before encountering any trap. Our results complete and generalise the ones by Amiet, Collevecchio, Scarsini and Zhong (2021), using a different approach.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

papers.title: Credible Sets of Overall Ranking of Entities
papers.abstract: Ranking, and inferences based on ranking of a set of entities, are important problems in numerous contexts. This is especially true in small area statistics where there may be only a limited amount of directly observed data from each entity or small area, while precise and accurate estimates of best or worst performing entities are needed for fund allocation, planning and policymaking, stakeholder advocacy, evaluation of welfare programs, and so on. However, ranks estimates constructed exclusively on point estimates of parameters lack uncertainty quantification, and may lead to imbalances and inequities when these are based on small sample sizes. We propose novel Bayesian approaches to address this problem. Our proposals result in partitions of the parameter space with posterior distribution driven partial ordering of the sets in a partition. This in turn translates to a coherent probability mass function over ranks for every entity, and a coherent probability mass function over entities for every rank. Our Bayesian algorithms significantly outperform the state-of-the-art non-Bayesian alternatives, and are amenable to inclusion of covariates in the model as well as borrowing strengths across small areas. We evaluate our proposed Bayesian algorithms in terms of accuracy and stability using a number of applications and a simulation study. Additionally, we develop a novel theoretical framework for inference and ranking problems involving a triangular array of Fay-Herriot models and data, and provide probabilistic guarantees of performances of the proposed Bayesian ranking algorithms.

papers.title: Ordinals and recursively defined functions on the reals
papers.abstract: We determine sufficient conditions under which certain recursively defined functions are well defined for all real inputs. Given a function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, call a decreasing sequence $x_1>x_2>x_3>\cdots$ "$f$-bad" if $f(x_1)>f(x_2)>f(x_3)>\cdots$, and call the function $f$ "ordinal decreasing" if there exist no infinite $f$-bad sequences. We prove the following result: Given ordinal decreasing functions $f,g_1,\ldots,g_k,s$ that are everywhere larger than $0$, define the recursive algorithm "$M(x)$: if $x<0$ return $f(x)$, else return $g_1(-M(x-g_2(-M(x-\cdots-g_k(-M(x-s(x)))\cdots))))$". Then $M(x)$ halts and is ordinal decreasing for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. The recursive algorithms $M$ and $M_n$ previously studied in the context of fusible numbers by Ericskon et al. (2022) and Bufetov et al. (2024), respectively, are special cases of this scheme. Moreover, given an ordinal decreasing function $f$, denote by $o(f)$ the ordinal height of the root of the tree of $f$-bad sequences. Then we prove that, for $k\ge 2$, the function $M(x)$ defined by the above algorithm satisfies $o(M)\leφ_{k-1}(γ+o(s)+1)$, where $γ$ is the smallest ordinal such that $\max\{o(s),o(f),o(g_1), \ldots, o(g_k)\} <φ_{k-1}(γ)$.

papers.title: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group. As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{τ_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $τ_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.

papers.title: Almost Sure Averaging for Fast-slow Stochastic Differential Equations via Controlled Rough Path
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the averaging method to a coupled system consisting of two stochastic differential equations which has a slow component driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with less regularity $1/3< H \leq 1/2$ and a fast dynamics under additive FBM with Hurst-index $1/3< \hat H \leq 1/2$. We prove that the solution of the slow component converges almost surely to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation using the approach of time discretization and controlled rough path. To do this, we employ the random dynamical system (RDS) to obtain a stationary solution by an exponentially attracting random fixed point of the RDS generated by the non-Markovian fast component.

papers.title: EnKF-C user guide
papers.abstract: EnKF-C provides a compact generic framework for off-line data assimilation into large-scale layered geophysical models with the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF). It is coded in C for GNU/Linux platform and can work either in EnKF, ensemble optimal interpolation (EnOI), or hybrid (EnKF/EnOI) modes.

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)γ$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{Ξ_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{Ξ_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{Ω_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{Ω_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ω_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ω_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $Γ(Ξ_{cc}^{*++}\toΞ_{cc}^{++}γ)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $Γ(Ξ_{cc}^{*+}\toΞ_{cc}^{+}γ)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $Γ(Ω_{cc}^{*+}\toΩ_{cc}^{+}γ)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
papers.abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verdú--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

papers.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
papers.abstract: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $ζ$-function $ζ_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $ζ$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.

papers.title: From Data to Wisdom: Rethinking AI Through an Epistemic Lens
papers.abstract: This paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture for AI (EAAI), a conceptual framework treating Data, Information, Knowledge, Understanding and Wisdom as five distinct but recursively interacting epistemic functions: observation, contextual interpretation, modeling and prediction, critical evaluation and informed judgment. Two observations motivate it: sequential readings of the Knowledge Pyramid obscure how these functions interact, and a targeted review of twelve Bayesian reference books finds that prior distributions are defined mathematically while "prior information" and "prior knowledge" are not consistently distinguished as epistemic categories. A Bayesian interpretation relates the likelihood, prior and posterior distributions, posterior prediction, model checking and decision analysis to the five functions, without limiting EAAI to Bayesian systems. Extending "prior" in an epistemic sense, the paper distinguishes five kinds of prior context that can shape the model, the likelihood, the prior, evaluation and action. Three worked applications -- quantitative financial risk, actuarial modeling in health insurance and agentic AI for medical reimbursement claims -- show how EAAI structures the analysis of model assumptions, evidence interpretation, validation, dependencies and decision consequences, separating the prediction of a risk, the appraisal of its reliability and the justification of action. It draws implications for AI and machine learning, including evaluation by function, treating intermediate model outputs as evidence open to challenge and separating generation from appraisal, and compares EAAI with work on DIKW, Bayesian workflow, AI evaluation and risk governance. Its contributions are an epistemic vocabulary with recursive relationships, a more accessible reading of Bayesian methodology, a typology of prior context and clearer methodological terminology

papers.title: Raysemble: Metric 3D Bone Reconstruction from a Single X-ray
papers.abstract: Raysemble reconstructs eight lumbar and pelvic bones from a single X-ray by separating shape and placement. Each 3D query samples regional and global features at its image projection. A shared decoder predicts normalized bone shapes. Predicted depth and camera geometry determine 3D centers and scales for resampling these shapes onto a common grid in millimeters. Evaluation uses 23 held-out patients with 43 CT scans, each generating one simulated anteroposterior radiograph. Without rigid alignment to CT,Raysemble leads 15 evaluated methods, averaging 65.24% Dice, 9.09 mm HD95, and 3.32 mm ASSD over three random seeds. With identical inputs, it improves Dice over VolumeNeRF by 5.86 percentage points.

papers.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than any baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors at least 1.6 times lower than Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.

papers.title: XBot-Omni: An Omni-Modal Model for Embodied Understanding and Interaction
papers.abstract: Embodied interaction requires an agent to integrate multimodal perception with verbal and nonverbal behaviors to effectively communicate its intentions, including speech, body motion, and facial expressions. We present XBot-Omni, a Thinker--Talker--Actor architecture that extends the Omni paradigm to robotic modalities, including body motion and facial expressions, with ``X'' representing the extensibility to robotic-specific modalities. The Thinker processes text, images, audio, and video to formulate contextually appropriate responses, which are then realized by the Talker and Actor through speech and coordinated bodily expressions, respectively. In this report, we innovatively introduce the concept of ``Actor'' as a dedicated component for embodied agents: a coordinated, streaming module that leverages the native representations of the Thinker and Talker within an end-to-end pipeline, introducing only modest latency overhead. This unified architecture enables multimodal generation conditioned on omni-modal inputs directly to prevent information loss in staged designs. We comprehensively evaluate XBot-Omni across seven benchmarks, demonstrating strong multimodal understanding capabilities on both general-domain and robot-centric videos, as well as high-quality, natural, and well-coordinated motion generation. Furthermore, our results validate its capability to generate embodied multimodal responses directly from omni inputs, meeting the diverse requirements of embodied interaction. XBot-Omni enables robots not only to perceive the omni world but also to express themselves through speech and bodily behaviors, extending Omni models from conversational interaction to embodied communication in physical environments.

papers.title: Faster Deterministic All-Pairs Shortest Paths with Real Edge Weights
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for all-pairs shortest paths in directed $n$-vertex graphs with arbitrary finite real edge weights and no negative cycles. It computes all distances in $O(n^{2.9929729})$ worst-case time, improving both the recent deterministic bound $O(n^{2.9997})$ and the Las Vegas expected-time bound $O(n^{2.993805})$. We use a model with exact real addition, subtraction and comparison at unit cost; auxiliary integer arithmetic and indexed memory access are charged at bit cost.

papers.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
papers.abstract: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

papers.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
papers.abstract: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

papers.title: Driving World Models Move the Camera, Not the Scene
papers.abstract: Plan-conditioned driving world models are used to compare candidate plans, so their forecast should change with the plan as the real scene would, yet widely used control metrics check only whether the camera follows the command. Recorded drives already contain real outcomes of plans that were never driven: retiming a log gives pose-matched images and LiDAR for other speeds, and a stereo rig records a laterally shifted view. Against these references, released world models move their camera but barely move the scene: their scene response, the share of the real change in distance that the forecast reproduces, reaches at most about a third of real video's, and the trajectory score cannot tell an executed speed command from an ignored one. Interventions inside the generator trace the failure to the plan's channel. The forecast geometry follows the context frames; once they carry the planned geometry, plan tokens add little. ReTime-Compose therefore delivers the plan as geometry, without training. It transports the frames of one logged-speed rollout to the planned cameras, and the frozen model completes only what no frame covers. Frozen generators then follow a 0.54 m lateral shift nearly as the real scene does on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and respond more than re-sampling to slow-down plans in three generators and to speed-up plans in two.

papers.title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
papers.abstract: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.
authors: J. P. A. M. de André

papers.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.abstract: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(ρ)=1+a^2/(4ρ^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=μ_r=n(ρ)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(ωa/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $πa^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

papers.title: Owned Edits to a Shared Decision Rule: Learning Private Exceptions as Typed, Gated, Withdrawable Weight Edits
papers.abstract: Organisations that apply the same published decision rule often hold private evidence that the rule is wrong for their own cases, and will not pool it. We describe a learning mechanism for that setting whose unit of change is an owned edit. The published rule is compiled exactly into a small ReLU network, a structured prior. Each party's learner searches a small typed space of declarations, a few named values such as subject, scope, form and size, and proposes one only when its own records pass a selection-aware evidence gate. The learning is that gated search around the prior. In two pre-registered analyses, on synthetic data whose 20 hidden truths were sampled from that typed space, the learner at 30 records per party was non-inferior, within 2 points, to all seven tuned baselines (a confined gradient learner, Ditto, FedRep, federated averaging, two pooled networks and pooled boosted trees), scoring 96.6% against 91.7% for the unchanged rule; a descriptive greedy ablation with no prior, over a separate space, scored 84.0%. In a third registered test, typed edits over a network trained on shared records beat that network alone by +5.4 points and the same edits over the published rule by +3.1; oracle-tuned fine-tuning and Ditto matched it at 30 records. An acceptance body recomputes each edit from its declaration and writes it into units reserved for that party, so by construction an edit changes no decision about any other subject, withdraws exactly, discloses at most log2 of the typed space's size in bits, and the artefact can hide nothing beyond its declared values; timing is not covered. We report where it loses: truths shared by all parties, relaxations, ten records, a pre-stated gate criterion that failed in both runs, and a language model given the records that decided about as accurately on one draw. On a rule-only base, a table of owned exceptions makes the same decisions.

papers.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
papers.abstract: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$) CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent optimal of the same output is polylogarithmic in $n$, specifically at most $O(\log^9{n})$. This is remarkable, as it shows an exponential speedup by switching to CGP. Our results shed light on the benefit and the compactness of the graph-based representation for programs, and on how CGP can navigate its search and fitness spaces efficiently. This is a first proven performance guarantee for CGP on an established benchmark problem. Experiments complement our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) models are often trained on nominal data using average-risk objectives, which emphasize dominant normal patterns. However, real time series can contain rare but valid nominal regimes that are underrepresented in the training distribution. We show that data-space flow matching can over-penalize such rare-normal windows and assign them anomaly scores comparable to those of true anomalies. To address this, we propose Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching (RT-FM), an unsupervised framework that uses a temporal variational autoencoder to estimate residual latent tailness and converts it into bounded, warmup-annealed weights for training a data-space flow matching model. Experiments on seven TSAD benchmarks show that RT-FM improves rare-normal coverage while preserving strong anomaly discrimination, substantially reducing false alarms on such windows and resulting in improved aggregate detection performance. The code is available at: https://github.com/trustAIoT/RT-FM_time-series-anomaly

papers.title: Beyond Service Discovery: Coverage Awareness in LLM-Driven Service Composition
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly support the automated discovery and composition of services. In federated data ecosystems, this creates new opportunities for reusing existing data products and transformation services when constructing service-based data exchange modeled as data-sharing pipelines. However, finding relevant reusable assets does not imply that the available assets are sufficient to satisfy a consumer request. In this paper, we distinguish reuse discovery, the ability to identify relevant published assets, from reuse coverage, the extent to which the available assets support the transformations required by a request. We further consider coverage awareness, the ability of a composition system to recognize insufficient coverage. We investigate this distinction using PipeFinder, an LLM-driven framework for composing data-sharing pipelines, and evaluate 99 consumer requests against a fixed catalogue of data products and transformation services. Our experiments show that relevant data products can be discovered reliably, while successful composition remains considerably more difficult. More importantly, when required transformation services are missing, the framework typically constructs a pipeline from the available services rather than recognizing that the request cannot be satisfied. Explicitly incorporating coverage checking into the planning procedure substantially improves recognition of such cases. These results suggest that coverage awareness should be treated as an explicit concern in LLM-driven service composition and cannot be assumed to follow from improved discovery or model capability.

papers.title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
papers.abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

papers.title: LENS: Replacing LayerNorm and Softmax in Transformers with Learnable Normalization States
papers.abstract: LayerNorm and attention Softmax are critical operations in Transformers. However, they cannot be efficiently mapped to General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) computations on hardware. Therefore, modern hardware accelerator designs, such as NPUs on ASIC/FPGA, consume a large amount of hardware resources or chip area to implement their specific arithmetic units. Building on previous work about LayerNorm, Softmax, and their alternatives, we introduce Learnable Normalization States (LENS), a framework that reformulates LayerNorm as tiny MLPs by abstracting a common structure from related methods and extends this method to Softmax, which moves more of the computation in Transformers to GEMM as a hardware-friendly architecture. We evaluate LENS on image classification with Vision Transformers (ViT) and autoregressive language modeling with Pythia models, including generalization tests on WikiText and LAMBADA. Across these tasks, LENS matches or exceeds baseline performance in several vision settings and retains most of the baseline performance in the remaining vision and language experiments. These findings may suggest that hand-designed normalization and attention functions are not the only choice as alternatives to LayerNorm and Softmax. LENS also provides a basis for exploring Transformer architectures for resource-limited accelerators.

papers.title: Sidewalk Stewards: A Visual Analytics Approach for Interactive Topology Repair of Sidewalk Networks
papers.abstract: Accurate pedestrian network data is foundational to urban accessibility, routing, and infrastructure planning, yet such data remains scarce and difficult to produce at scale. Automated extraction pipelines have made significant strides by leveraging computer vision to derive sidewalk networks from aerial imagery, and have seen real-world adoption by municipalities seeking cost-effective inventory solutions. Yet, these pipelines consistently produce topological errors (e.g., disconnected components, dangling edges, missed connections, malformed intersections) that undermine the utility of the extracted networks for routing and accessibility analysis. Correcting these errors requires situated human judgment that global automated repair strategies cannot replicate, yet practitioners currently lack dedicated tools to support this work efficiently. We present Sidewalk Stewards, a visual analytics system that bridges the gap between automated extraction and a deployment-ready pedestrian network. Sidewalk Stewards detects candidate topology errors, supports interactive user-guided correction through coordinated spatial views, and provides real-time quality feedback as edits are applied. We evaluate Sidewalk Stewards through a comparative user study, case studies across cities, and a quantitative evaluation. Compared with conventional workflows, the system facilitates error identification and enables faster and more complete correction. The case studies illustrate the workflow across different urban contexts, and the quantitative evaluation shows that a small number of user corrections can enhance multiple sidewalk quality metrics. Sidewalk Stewards is available at urbantk.org/sidewalk.

papers.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
papers.abstract: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $χ^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. The complete solver fits on a small, low-cost FPGA and contains no multiplier anywhere in its datapath, placing nonlinear optical modelling within reach of embedded and autonomous platforms rather than of high-performance computers.

papers.title: Phase Structure and Thermodynamic Geometry of STU Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics of four-dimensional STU black holes, a family of charged solutions of gauged N = 8, SO(8) supergravity, from the perspective of geometric thermodynamics. We focus on non-rotating solutions carrying pairwise-equal charges, obtaining closed-form expressions for the thermodynamic quantities directly in terms of the physical charges, and use them to determine the equation of state and associated phase structure. We also construct the Ruppeiner geometry for the STU black hole, taking the temperature and thermodynamic volume as fluctuation variables, and study its renormalized curvature as a probe of the black hole microstructure. We find a rich phase structure with two critical points present whenever the charge ratio is sufficiently large, and identify regions in parameter space associated with attractive and repulsive microscopic interactions.

papers.title: Exceptional structure and Lifshitz criticality in a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain
papers.abstract: We study an exactly solvable non-Hermitian $N$-site Kitaev chain with unequal pair-creation and pair-annihilation amplitudes and vanishing intersite hopping. We show that the chain supports an exceptional point (EP) at which all the many-body energies collapse to zero and the largest Jordan block grows quadratically with $N$. By constructing an explicit positive metric for the associated $N$-dimensional one-body problem which admits an extension to the full many-body Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that this EP collapse can be approached through a continuous quasi-Hermitian path in the parameter space. Further, in a different regime with onsite energies alternating between two unequal positive values, we show that pairing amplitudes of opposite signs can lead to crossings between ground states of opposite fermion parity within a quasi-Hermitian regime. Their accumulation in the thermodynamic limit produces a Lifshitz transition, characterized by particle-/hole-pocket formation, quadratic critical dispersion, and a nonanalytic ground-state energy density. We show that this transition remains separated from the EP boundary and ceases to exist for balanced real pairing.

papers.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) affects millions of US adults. Primary care-based screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment (SBIRT) is a leading strategy for identifying heavy drinking early, but access to primary care, screening, and specialty treatment differs markedly across subgroups. Whether scaling SBIRT and expanding treatment capacity narrows or widens these differences is unknown and cannot feasibly be tested in a randomized trial. We present AUDTxSim (AUD Treatment Simulation), a stochastic, spatially explicit, individual-based model of alcohol use, AUD, SBIRT, and specialty treatment for the adult populations of California and Texas. Agents represent every adult in synthetic populations of the two states (28.0 and 19.3 million adults), each geo-located to a Census tract and linked to nearby treatment facilities. In daily time steps, the model simulates: (1) annual transitions among eight alcohol use and AUD states; (2) healthcare visits, screening, brief intervention, and referral; (3) treatment seeking, standalone medication for AUD, mutual help, and requests for hospitalization, residential, or outpatient care; (4) a treatment manager that allocates individuals to facilities by preference, geography, and capacity, with telehealth substitution and waitlists; and (5) treatment progression, stepdown between levels of care, and post-treatment mutual help. It is implemented in Python with Repast4Py to run in parallel on a computing cluster. Once calibrated to state, rural-urban, and demographic targets for healthcare visits, heavy drinking and AUD prevalence, and mortality, AUDTxSim will project population-level and subgroup-specific effects of alternative SBIRT reach and treatment capacity scenarios on AUD prevalence, treatment receipt, and mortality. We report the model structure, decision logic, data sources, and calibration plan.

papers.title: Measuring Coherence in Predictive Models
papers.abstract: Many sequential decision-making procedures, such as active learning, implicitly assume that a model's current predictions agree with those it expects to make after updating on new data, a property we call coherence. Most models in use do not update by exact conditioning and are not guaranteed to be coherent, which can lead to worse decisions. Yet there is currently no general way to measure incoherence or to tell when it matters. We develop tools to measure incoherence and characterise when it affects decisions. We introduce the incoherence ratio, an MMD-based measure of how far any updating procedure departs from coherence, computed only from the procedure's own predictions and updates, and accompany it with an anytime-valid test of coherence. In Bayesian experimental design, acquisition objectives that are equivalent for coherent models choose different data under every approximate model we study, and the incoherence ratio tracks how far incoherence distorts them. We also introduce action coherence, which captures only the incoherence that changes a decision. What a resulting disagreement costs, however, is determined primarily by predictive accuracy. Sequential decisions depend on how a model updates as well as on what it predicts, so coherence, like accuracy, should be checked rather than assumed.

papers.title: High-Speed Forward and Reverse Tractor-Trailer Driving with Learned Vehicle Dynamics
papers.abstract: Tractor-trailer systems are difficult to control, especially unstable during reverse motion, and their dynamics depend on difficult-to-measure factors, including road friction and suspension coefficients. We introduce a learned dynamics model for tractor-trailer control and compare it with a reduced-order dynamics model with Fiala tire forces as an analytic baseline. Specifically, we compare a model predictive path integral (MPPI) controller that uses the learned dynamics model to an MPPI controller that uses the analytic model, as well as to three additional baseline controllers. In the main closed-loop tracking experiments across four simulated environments, MPPI with learned dynamics achieves mean speeds closer to the target magnitudes and lower root-mean-square (RMS) hitch angles than MPPI with the analytic model at every tested setpoint, with higher completion rates in seven of eight reverse configurations.

papers.title: Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

papers.title: Maximum Scores and Treatment Feedback in Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract: Hospitals use repeated risk scores to decide when to send an alert. Some evaluations summarize these scores by their maximum and use the maximum as the running variable in a regression discontinuity (RD) design. The maximum shows correctly whether a patient was ever alerted. However, it can include scores recorded after an earlier alert has already changed care. In this paper, we study what the maximum-score RD estimates when an earlier intervention changes a later score. We use a two-assessment model and derive a formula that splits the RD contrast into the causal effect and a composition term. When feedback moves scores in one direction, the composition term equals the relative jump in the density of the maximum at the cutoff times a prognostic contrast. Therefore, an exactly continuous density means no bias, and the population density jump bounds the bias. Valid inference on the jump turns this into a confidence bound under a stated sensitivity assumption. Within this model, bias behind a continuous density requires feedback in both directions. For this case, we bound bias by total boundary movement and construct conservative confidence sets for binary outcomes under explicit sensitivity and smoothness assumptions. We give closed forms for independent uniform scores and for correlated Gaussian scores. In one example, a true risk reduction of four percentage points appears as a one-point increase. Simulations confirm the formulas. Narrower bandwidths, robust bias correction, and machine-learning covariate adjustment do not remove the bias. A fuzzy RD on the first score recovers the causal effect when early and late treatment have the same effect. Our results concern how the running variable is built. We do not assess any published clinical study.

papers.title: Unreasonable Confidence from Simulator Misspecification: Directional Robustness on the SPEED+ Sim-to-Real Benchmark
papers.abstract: Vision-based navigation systems for orbit must be trained almost entirely on synthetic imagery, because real labelled images of a given spacecraft in flight rarely exist. Benchmarks like SPEED+ are built for that situation: the training set comes from a simulator, and the test sets are real images of a satellite mockup under two kinds of lighting. That simulator approximates how light reflects off mylar and aluminium, and like every scientific simulator it is misspecified. Its error is radiometric, since it misses the specular highlights, hard shadows and sensor saturation common in real images. We probe the resulting synthetic-to-real gap, the central risk for such systems, with a deliberately simple monocular pose estimator. In a 2x2 study of backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation, trained on synthetic images and tested on both real hardware-in-the-loop domains, we find three things. (1) The model does not know it is failing: regions conformally calibrated to 90% on synthetic data cover only 9-15% of rotation errors on sunlamp and 21-38% on lightbox, so a wrong pose carries the confidence of a correct one. (2) Transfer is asymmetric: scaling data and features improved synthetic rotation error from 1.65 to 1.03 rad but moved the harshly lit sunlamp domain by only 0.05 rad, under twice its seed s.d., whereas adapting the backbone's last stage carried 63-83% of its extra synthetic gain to both real domains. (3) Once the backbone adapts, augmentation helps only in the direction it models: our photometric stack improved the diffusely lit lightbox domain from 1.17 to 0.99 rad on every seed but moved sunlamp no more than seed-to-seed variation, while with the backbone frozen it helped sunlamp more. Every post-review experiment was pre-registered, and the code, per-image predictions and pre-registration record are at https://github.com/lokindoo/spacecraft-pose-estimation.

papers.title: Course-Referenced Lateral Control of Trail-Following Convoys: String Stability and Adaptive Feedforward under Load Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Vehicles in a convoy can steer along the GNSS trails of the vehicles ahead when lane markings are unavailable, as on snow covered roads.
