papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of global pose synchronization for heterogeneous multiple rigid-body systems evolving on the matrix Lie group $\SE(3)$. We first construct a new potential function on $\SE(3) \times \mathbb{R}$ with a generalized non-diagonal weighting matrix, together with a set of switching variables governed by continuous-discrete hybrid dynamics. Based on this new potential function and these switching variables, we propose a distributed hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative pose on $\SE(3)$ and group velocity measurements, endowed with global asymptotic stability guarantees. We then further propose a distributed velocity-free hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative and absolute pose measurements, without requiring group velocity measurements, while preserving global asymptotic stability. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed distributed hybrid control schemes.

papers.title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
papers.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used to customize large language models, but third-party adapters create supply-chain backdoor risks with under 1% modified parameters. Recent analytical null-space and subspace projection defenses report near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR), equating static silence with erasure. We audit subspace-projection defenses across four scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B), three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5-1.8B, Spark-X2.6-4B), and five trigger families (suffix, natural phrase, prefix/in-sentence, double-negation syntax, and composite triggers). Statically, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection cuts ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard suites and 70.3% to 0.0% on 1,000 uncontaminated prompts (p = 3.055e-299) in under 5 s. By Theorem 1 (11,880/11,880 module-sample pairs), low-rank bottleneck amplification aligns benign polite-suffix probes with u_1(B) (median cosine 0.8934-0.9705), reaching 0.0% ASR without trigger knowledge. However, static suppression is not erasure. Under 5-sample reactivation, single-round weight-editing baselines rebound to 91.7%-100.0% ASR in Epoch 1 (Fine-Pruning, ANP, NEEDLE, LoRA-Patch; 48.7% for single-round dual projection) and 100.0% by Epoch 2. Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 prove single-sided projection leaves non-zero gradients along u_1 across 168/168 modules (27.2x-31.1x above random expectation), while Haar orthogonal rotation shows Epoch-2 immunity depends on semantic alignment rather than Frobenius norm. Guided by Theorems 1-2, we propose Single-Shot Rank-k Dual-Subspace Erasure (DSE) and Benign Subspace Anchoring (DSE-BA), achieving 0.0% static ASR and 0.0% Epoch-1 reactivation across all five trigger families and Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B, while cutting Epoch-2 ASR to 25.0% (43.33% +/- 2.49% on 50 prompts x 3 seeds) and benign PPL to 6.54.

papers.title: That Time of the Year Again: Government Pay Revisions in the Aggregate Economy
papers.abstract: Public pay is set by law in nominal terms, so inflation erodes its real value between legal acts until the government revises it. I model each revision as the choice of a forward-looking government, shaped by two costs that push in opposite directions. A fixed cost of acting makes revisions large and rare, whereas a convex cost of financing the increase at once makes them small and frequent. Through the budget, each revision also moves debt and the risk of fiscal stress under which the next one is made. In the documented pay decisions of eleven countries, pay set at discretion erodes against prices and private earnings and is restored in discrete steps, every cut was decided during market stress or an adjustment program, and court rulings drove a wedge between the cuts legislated, the cuts paid and the cuts that lasted. Estimated on the legal acts, the model reproduces the documented paths of pay in most countries when data and simulations are measured the same way. In Portugal's estimated model, the savings that the Treasury requires once spreads rise produce the cuts, the debt overhang holds pay down after the crisis, and a court that strikes cuts after they take effect invites cuts it will strike. Review of cuts before they took effect would have lowered the social cost of Portugal's crisis relative to review after the fact, and partial indexation would have paid in Bangladesh unless its automatic increases were costly to finance.

papers.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
papers.abstract: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

papers.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
papers.abstract: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit spatial and temporal feature differences offer a way to capture this variation, but also respond to natural texture and motion, motivating their joint interpretation with appearance features. We investigate whether combining multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance representations improves detection across both forgery categories. We introduce Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector. The residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames. The semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43\%, outperforming seven compared detectors. When trained on facial manipulations alone, MARS achieves 93.99\% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50\% on DF26, demonstrating transfer to generated videos without generated-video training data. MARS also provides signed patch and frame contributions, whose faithfulness we evaluate through controlled spatial and temporal removal against random controls. MARS is publicly available for research: Project page: https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mars/ Github: https://github.com/VectorInstitute/mars

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear and quadratic gravity
papers.abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity and general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory, the dimension, and the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile, or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$ dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We compare the two considered theories and study relations between their solution sets. We further examine conformal relations, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and so is the Weyl squared action (that reduces to Weyl conformal gravity in $n=4$), as a particular example of quadratic gravity couplings. Explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

papers.title: From Token Bills to Benchmark Weeks: Making Auto-Research for Data Systems Verifiable and Affordable
papers.abstract: AI auto-research is poised to forge bespoke data systems, from key-value stores and indexes to query engines, each engineered for a specific workload and hardware platform. Yet this promise rests on fragile ground. An agent optimizes what it can measure, not necessarily what users need. Natural-language requirements leave ample room for specification gaming, producing systems that blaze through benchmarks while silently losing updates or violating consistency. Worse, each research iteration consumes tokens, while validating a candidate under real concurrency, memory pressure, and failure conditions can stretch the entire research process into weeks. In this paper, we envision a more cost-efficient and verifiable approach to auto-research. Precise and composable specifications anchor the search, lightweight performance critics prune costly dead ends, and falsification and deductive verification make correctness an integral part of the process rather than an afterthought. By treating correctness, performance, research time, and token cost as equally important objectives, we aim to transform AI-generated data systems from plausible artifacts into trustworthy, production-grade systems whose behavior can be understood, audited, and ultimately relied upon.

papers.title: Derived invariance of holomorphic two-forms and homological motives of stably holomorphically symplectic varieties
papers.abstract: Let $Φ:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb C$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $Θ^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $Φ$. We prove that $Θ^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove that being stably holomorphically symplectic is a derived invariant, where a smooth projective variety is called stably holomorphically symplectic if it is a direct factor of a smooth projective holomorphic symplectic variety. For derived-equivalent varieties in this class, we construct an isomorphism of rational homological motives as unital algebra objects. In particular, their graded rational cohomology algebras are isomorphic compatibly with the Hodge structures.

papers.title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
papers.abstract: We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $η$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences. For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $η$-constant and the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $η$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class. The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.

papers.title: MOSU2: Long-range Navigation System with Multi-modal Scene Understanding
papers.abstract: Robots that travel long distances through public outdoor spaces must do more than avoid obstacles: they must remain on terrain suited to their mobility and decide when to proceed, yield, or detour around pedestrians, cyclists, vehicles, traffic signals, and temporary restrictions. These decisions are difficult because their correctness often depends on how a scene evolves, such as whether an approaching car is slowing or a cyclist will cross the robot's path. Vision-language models (VLMs) can interpret such cues, but they reason over images that lack metric geometry and motion. Supplying this evidence at every step is too slow for real-time navigation, and hand-crafted triggers cannot anticipate the open-ended variety of outdoor situations. We present MOSU2, a long-range navigation system with two-stage trajectory selection, in which first-stage contextual reasoning determines when additional evidence is needed and what to retrieve. Only when an interaction remains unresolved does the first stage trigger the second stage to retrieve geometric and dynamic information and align it with scene context to make navigation decisions. Building on MOSU, MOSU2 follows routes from GPS-based route planning and filters candidate trajectories through multi-modal traversability analysis before selecting a trajectory to move the robot. In real-world experiments spanning stop gestures, construction sites, crosswalks, and roads shared with vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians, MOSU2 raises mean navigation success from 61.8% to 94.2% and condition-detection accuracy from 72.2% to 91.4% over its single-image predecessor, at about 2.2 times its mean decision latency. Project website: https://jinggm.github.io/mosu2/

papers.title: Integer Programming Parametrized by Imbalanced Circuit Packing
papers.abstract: We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

papers.title: FG-DSA: Frequency-Guided Depthwise Separable Attention for Efficient Dense Prediction
papers.abstract: Dense prediction and generative modeling remain challenging in resource-constrained environments, particularly because repeated downsampling can lead to the loss of spatial details and less accurate object boundaries. Although attention mechanisms have been widely adopted to address semantic ambiguity, preserving high-frequency information while maintaining computational efficiency remains an important challenge. To address this issue, we propose Frequency-Guided Depthwise Separable Attention for Efficient Dense Prediction (FG-DSA), a framework that integrates frequency-domain information into lightweight vision architectures for dense visual understanding and generation. Specifically, FG-DSA uses a 2D Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based high-pass filtering module to guide spatial attention, aiming to retain fine-grained features and improve object-boundary representation. Experimental results show that FG-DSA can improve boundary-related performance in semantic segmentation under the evaluated setting. Beyond discriminative tasks, we also examine its application in a generative U-Net for single-step image restoration. The results suggest that incorporating FG-DSA can enhance reconstruction quality and help preserve high-frequency details.

papers.title: Safe by Accident: Crash-Testing LLM-Written Code
papers.abstract: Evaluations of LLM-written code run it once, in one environment, and credit the code with whatever passes. We show that this credit can belong to the environment. We crashed LLM-written backend code just before each database, file and email call, re-ran it as an operator would, and judged the result under two transaction modes of Python's sqlite3: the default, in which the library quietly opens a transaction, and autocommit, in which it does not. Across 9,100 solutions from ten models on 24 backend tasks, more than half (54%) of the database code that survives every crash in the default mode is left half-updated in autocommit mode. This holds for every model, and it hides in ordinary code, including with conn: blocks that look like transactions but open none. Telling the model that its connection is in autocommit mode does not change what the local code models write, while the API models' unsafe share falls by 30 points. Asking for crash safety helps every model, and strong models repair nearly all unsafe code, but often write safe code only when asked. Thus, much of the crash safety that LLM-written database code appears to have is borrowed from the library rather than designed into it, and a second test under a less forgiving configuration reveals the difference.

papers.title: What extraction cannot slim, and whether function injection can: a pre-registered study of 580 Java repositories
papers.abstract: A method of 26 code lines or more reads as a Long Method, and Extract Method is the usual fix. Some long methods have no single-exit fix: a return cannot leave an extracted piece, a piece hands back one value, and some methods are knotted so that every cut is blocked. Function injection, as the OfficeFloor framework does it, cuts differently: each piece becomes a function the framework injects and sequences, an early return ends a function, and a function hands on several values. The framework's author pre-registered a test of whether it takes apart what extraction cannot. A stratified random sample of 580 open-source Java repositories, each pinned before AI coding assistants were in general use, was scanned by released tools whose cost models were fixed before the sample was drawn: 3,026,902 methods, 168,466 of them long. Single-exit extraction cannot slim 22.9% of the long methods. The registered hypothesis, that at least a quarter of those stuck methods are ones only function injection takes apart, is refuted: 22.2% (95% CI 20.3 to 24.4). Nearly half of the stuck methods are early-return methods the plan counts as conventionally fixable, and the split takes three in four of those apart as they stand. Where extraction would do, the split chooses injection and costs less for 29.0% against extraction wrapped as one function and 17.3% against plain extraction, almost always as a straight sequence of functions. An exploratory reading of the quarter of the stuck methods that neither takes apart finds a third of it tables and literals, long for their data rather than their logic, and most of the rest blocked by a jump inside a loop, by a nested statement too large to cut, or by values too many for any cut. Three registered studies are proposed: the classes as rules in the tools, a refinement per class, and the same measures on code written with AI assistants.

papers.title: Continual Instruction Tuning for LLM-based Management of Continuum Resources
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for resource management across the Cloud-Edge continuum. However, embedding LLMs directly inside latency-sensitive control loops places inference latency, execution jitter, and hallucination risks on the critical path. This study argues for a different use of LLMs: a continually instruction-tuned intent compiler that runs once per management intent or declared context change, above a fast, deterministic tactical controller that handles all low-latency runtime actions. We formulate intent compilation as a continual instruction tuning problem, because management intents arrive sequentially and accumulate while infrastructure and workload contexts drift. Unlike recent LLM-based management frameworks, our design scores the model's outputs by execution, so that catastrophic forgetting can be measured in the executed objective of the underlying controller. On a continuum simulator with a 2B backbone and parameter-efficient adapters, preliminary results show that naive sequential tuning forgets earlier intents in the executed objective, that replay of stored examples nearly prevents this forgetting, and that the tuned compact compiler performs on par with simpler translators while being more robust than a grammar parser to rephrased intents. Code and data are available at https://github.com/lilanpei/continuum-intent-compiler.

papers.title: STAIRS: Staging the Inverse Problem via Admissible-Support Scheduling for Unrolled MRI Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Accelerated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) forms images from incomplete Fourier measurements, shifting acquisition burden to computational reconstruction. Deep unrolled networks interleave learned regularization and data consistency, yet typically estimate the full unmeasured spectrum at every cascade. We propose STAIRS (Staging the Inverse Problem via Admissible-Support Scheduling), which projects intermediate reconstructions onto nested Fourier supports that expand to the full spectrum and conditions each update on its support transition. Conditional increments of a regularized log-determinant score of training covariance define a normalized spectral coordinate, accounting for dependencies between newly and previously admitted frequencies. Dyadic targets allocate larger coordinate increments to earlier cascades and are mapped to fixed supports before training, enabling coarse-to-fine reconstruction with unchanged sampling masks and data consistency. On fastMRI and Stanford2D, STAIRS improves matched Transformer (HUMUSNet) and convolutional (NAFNet) backbones in single- and multi-coil reconstruction, including radiologist-annotated pathology regions. It also outperforms predictor-based progression with lower parameter overhead and inference latency. Stage-wise analysis shows repeated error correction by projection and lower intermediate reconstruction errors than the backbones alone throughout support expansion. Ablations favor dyadic allocation over uniform expansion for square and line-band supports and over manual front-loading for square windows. Support projection alone improves reconstruction, and transition conditioning strengthens the gain. Cross-dataset evaluation shows improvements for both backbones in both directions. Support allocation thus complements regularizer design in unrolled MRI reconstruction.

papers.title: Modeling the Joint Distribution of Box Score Statistics: A Gaussian Copula Approach
papers.abstract: What is the probability that LeBron James records at least 27 points, 7 rebounds, and 7 assists tonight? While an interesting statistical question by itself, the rise of sports betting and multi-leg parlays has made answering this question increasingly relevant. However, coming up with an estimated likelihood is tricky, since box score statistics aren't independent. We estimate the joint probability that a player reaches a combination of thresholds in points, assists, and rebounds using a Gaussian copula, fit separately for each player using only their previous games. We compare it with two benchmarks: the product of the empirical marginal probabilities (i.e. assuming independence) and the empirical frequency of the joint event. Across ~22,000 player-observations, the Gaussian copula performs on par or better than either benchmark at lower threshold levels, with large gains at high joint exceedance levels. Because it is generative, the model also allows for probabilistic calculations for combinations that a player has rarely or never produced.

papers.title: From PAC bounds on the generalization error to PAC bounds on the parameter estimation error
papers.abstract: Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) bounds on the generalization error, the difference between the true prediction error and the empirical prediction error, are an established tool in statistical machine learning, and there have been several extensions of these bounds to dynamical systems. In parallel, in recent years, there has been growing interest in finite-sample bounds for parameter estimation error in system identification. The latter bounds tend to be algorithm-specific, relying on reformulating the identification algorithm as a least-squares regression problem. This is in contrast to classical PAC bounds, which are algorithm-agnostic and can be applied to any identification algorithm based on minimizing a cost function involving the empirical loss. In this paper, we show how oracle bounds derived from PAC bounds can be used to obtain finite-sample bounds for dynamical systems. As an illustration of this approach, we present finite-sample parameter-estimation bounds for linear and bilinear systems with bounded inputs and noise. These bounds apply to identification algorithms based on minimizing the empirical loss function.

papers.title: Generative Search and Recommendation at Shopify
papers.abstract: Search and recommendation at Shopify require retrieving relevant products from a changing catalog of billions of products under strict latency constraints. We present SID-LLM, which casts both tasks as generating semantic IDs: short sequences of content-derived tokens representing products. We jointly pre-train SID-LLM on catalog and behavioral data, giving search and recommendation a shared representation and training objective. We show that reinforcement learning further improves judged search relevance. Furthermore, distillation from task-specific experts improves recommendation quality over joint supervised fine-tuning without a statistically detected loss in search quality. Finally, for efficient serving, we pair multi-token prediction with a lightweight ranker, improving retrieval quality over our autoregressive baseline while reducing latency. We evaluate SID-LLM both as a standalone retriever and as a component of Shopify's production search and recommendation systems. As a standalone search system, SID-LLM achieves quality comparable to Shopify's existing multi-model search stack while meeting production latency requirements. Integrating SID-LLM into the search and recommendation stacks provides significant gains in both offline evaluations and online A/B tests. Together, these results demonstrate the practical value of semantic-ID generation as a unified approach to product discovery at scale.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.abstract: Process tomography on a stabilizer code compares the logical channel of a repetition code against a reference channel, through a decoder almost always fixed to the standard minimum-weight one. We ask how many physical single-qubit Pauli gates that decoder needs when the measurement basis is fixed, the constraint under which the count is a resource rather than a bookkeeping artefact. Exhaustive enumeration of every recovery design at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ qubits, each rank decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order decoding and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full minimum-weight decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, never on which, so the design problem splits into a budget and a placement; but the placement decides identifiability, and more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and the precision curve at $n=3$ is U-shaped under a calibration-residual floor. At the median of $40$ working points the three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder, and better at every one of them; the factor belongs to the point, the ordering does not. Because that advantage requires choosing the placement at the point, we also certify a floor that needs no such choice: two three-gate placements in parallel lose no direction that either sees, and cost at most $\sqrt{2}$ in worst-parameter deviation at equal total shots, giving recoverability at every point for at most twice the shots. At a unit per-component error the pair reaches a $10\,\mathrm{mrad}$ worst-parameter target in $\sim10^{5}$ shots at a median working point. Finally, the optimal designs are not covariant under chain reversal: on the collision locus of arXiv:2610.19779 they separate the mirror pair by $1.3\times10^{-3}$ while leaving the Jacobian at full rank.

papers.title: CardioLM: A multilingual suite of small language models for the cardiology domain
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular care generates large volumes of clinical free-text documentation in local languages. However, clinical natural language processing (NLP) resources remain concentrated in English, and no existing benchmark is cardiology-specific, multilingual, and broad in entity coverage. Methods: We present two contributions. The first is CardioCCC, a corpus of 508 cardiology case reports originally published in Spanish and extended to Czech, Dutch, English, Italian, Romanian, and Swedish through machine translation, annotation projection, and clinician review, with annotations covering diseases, symptoms, procedures, and medications. The second is CardioLM, comprising CardioBERTa, a set of language-specific encoders obtained by continued pretraining on cardiology and biomedical corpora, and CardioNER, a set of named entity recognition (NER) models fine-tuned on CardioCCC. Results: Cardiology-specific pretraining reduced pseudo-perplexity by up to a factor of eight, yet changed strict span-level F1 by at most 0.04, with benefits concentrated in languages whose backbones lacked biomedical coverage. The jointly trained multilingual XLM-RoBERTa-large models achieved the best strict F1 in nearly every language and entity type, exceeding the strongest monolingual system by up to 0.13 F1. A large share of residual errors concerned boundary detection: relaxed matching recovered 0.10-0.23 F1 for disease, procedure, and symptom, but only 0.01-0.07 for medication. Clinicians rated CardioNER well above a rule- and dictionary-based baseline, with the mean rating across entity types rising from 26% to 73%. Conclusions: Specialty-specific pretraining is not the decisive factor for downstream entity recognition, whereas multilingual joint training yields the strongest results in nearly all settings and a simpler deployment path for multi-country clinical information extraction.

papers.title: Detecting Is Not Counting: CountScan and the Limits of Certifying Watermark Matches
papers.abstract: Writing assistants can watermark the words they suggest. In an audit, when a school or publisher asks the provider of such an assistant about a submitted report, the provider checks how many positions of a passage match tokens its service returned, without having retained request logs. A watermark test shows that such matches exist, not how many. We introduce CountScan, a scan that turns per-token watermark evidence into lower bounds on the number of matches, valid for every passage at once and after key-blind editing by the writer, at a cost logarithmic in the text length. Since different hidden histories can release the same text with different numbers of matches, no valid count can certify more than they all share. In explicit models of the writing interface, in which the writer may request, retry and discard suggestions, retain their own draft and edit under a request cap, we compute this limit exactly and show that a variant of CountScan attains it. In simulations it stays valid and, under a hard history, certifies at least 2.5% of the positions in 100% of documents with 10^4 positions.

papers.title: Data-Driven Configuration of Protective Separation Zones in Collaborative Robot Cells from Operator Occupancy
papers.abstract: The protective separation zone of a collaborative robot cell is commonly dimensioned for a worst case that disregards where the operator is actually present during the task. This paper presents a camera-based, data-driven method that configures this zone from observed operator occupancy. Operator positions accumulated over several production shifts are aggregated into an occupancy heatmap, from which a protective field is derived that trades off the achievable robot velocity against the required safety distance, following the speed and separation monitoring principle of ISO/TS 15066. The resulting configuration is advisory, that is, reviewed within the risk assessment rather than applied autonomously to the robot controller. The method, which builds on a pose-based perception pipeline with activity recognition, was evaluated in two operational cells at two industrial partners, where the protective field could be reduced by approximately 17% and a productivity increase of 9% was measured. However, adoption proved to depend on more than the demonstrated gain alone.

papers.title: Dispersive Corrections to Electromagnetic Energy and Power Flux Are Imprints of Eliminated Degrees of Freedom
papers.abstract: In a spatially dispersive medium the electromagnetic energy and flux are given by the frequency and wave-vector derivatives of the constitutive parameters, a result known as the Agranovich--Ginzburg (AG) formulas. Here, we clarify the physical meaning of the derivative terms in these relations and show that they measure the energy and flux carried by the degrees of freedom of the internal field-matter dynamics that the Maxwellian constitutive description hides. We construct an extended state-space model of such dynamics for a wide class of temporally and spatially dispersive media, from which the Maxwellian constitutive relations follow upon elimination of the internal variables, the effective material operator resulting from the Schur complement of the eliminated internal block. A congruence identity relates this complement to the extended state-space description, which allows us to extend the AG formulas to general bianisotropic media and to establish the conditions of their validity in the presence of dissipation. The AG dispersive corrections are thus the imprints of the eliminated degrees of freedom rather than independent constitutive postulates. They hold for fields driven at arbitrary real frequency and wave vector, and not only for eigenmodes, provided that the sources act on the fields alone and that any dissipation is carried by the electromagnetic subsystem. We verify the construction on the Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models, the last of which describes a nonlocal metal. Additionally, a bianisotropic omega-medium and a capacitively loaded wire medium are treated in the Supplemental Material.

papers.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups. A companion project on Lean v4.35 imports that library's generation theorem for the model and proves, with no hypotheses, that $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ is isomorphic to the model, compatibly with the Griess algebras, and that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.06.

papers.title: Do Search-Augmented Recommenders Use the Latest Search Episode?
papers.abstract: When a user returns to a recommendation feed after searching, does the latest search episode help rank the next item? Aggregate ranking gains leave open whether search-augmented recommenders use the latest search at prediction time or benefit from broader search state and representation learning. FocalSwap is a counterfactual audit that masks or replaces the latest episode or the full search history while holding the target, candidates, recommendation history, and trained scorer fixed. A planted-signal test and GenSAR's native search-item prediction task verify that FocalSwap detects known search dependence. In proxy analyses, KuaiSAR's routing gain falls below the shuffled threshold, and Qilin's clearest matched-search advantage appears at high taxonomy overlap. The primary comparisons for SESRec and UniSAR do not establish a positive ranking gain from the latest search episode alone. For the full search history, the estimated contribution depends on the control. On 66,139 shared instances across three UniSAR checkpoints, neutral masking consistently lowers mean reciprocal rank (RR). Replacing the history with observed searches matched on category and activity profile changes 44.1 to 44.8 percent of target ranks, yet the original history has little average advantage. In the primary assignment, matched replacements yield mean RR 0.002770 to 0.006604 higher than neutral masking across checkpoints. The adjusted intervals for this difference lie above zero under the primary assignment and all five alternative assignments per checkpoint. Search audits should specify which inputs changed and what replaced them, and report both how often ranks move and how much the original search helps.

papers.title: Debiased Conditional Independence Tests for Causal Effects
papers.abstract: We propose robust tests for causal effects on potentially high-dimensional outcomes where there may be selection into treatment. These tests measure conditional independence of outcomes from treatment assignment by asking whether treatment can be predicted from outcomes more accurately than from covariates alone. We design three such tests of conditional independence. First, we propose a conditional randomization test based on an inverse propensity weighted mean squared error test statistic. If the propensity score is known, the test controls size in finite samples. Second, we propose a double-residualization approach, where we partial out covariate effects from both treatment and outcome-based treatment predictions, and test whether the correlation between the residuals is zero. Third, we propose a test based on an augmented inverse propensity weighted estimator built around doubly robust, Neyman-orthogonal population moments that are necessary and sufficient for conditional independence. Simulations show that all three tests improve power over a joint Wald test based on a seemingly unrelated regression across many non-linear settings, particularly under heavy tails, outliers, mixtures, heterogeneous effects, and effects with opposite signs.

papers.title: Discourse Analysis of Legislative Bill Discussions
papers.abstract: Legislative hearings are distinct communication events with their own human recognizable structure and logic, yet they have been analyzed as distinct phenomena beyond their transcripts. Understanding legislative hearings at a deeper level is a major step in analyzing the work and power relationships within democratic bodies. In this work, we present a novel end-to-end pipeline for parsing rhetorical structures from legislative committee hearings with the goal of improving legislative discourse analysis and democratic accountability. We also propose a rhetorical structure grammar and find that 74.71% of California state bill discussions in our dataset can be parsed with this grammar. We evaluate our pipeline with two utterance section classifiers on a random subset of over 2619 annotated utterances corresponding to 100 hearings. We find that a logistic regression-based classifier with grammar-based output masking and utterance tag smoothing outperforms more complex models, achieving an F1 score of 59.0% against our ground truth discourse section labels.

papers.title: Relative cohomology and base-change
papers.abstract: In this note we prove a simple generalization of cohomology and base-change which seems to be missing from standard sources. We illustrate its usefulness by providing an alternative proof of a result of Ishimura on descent of vector bundles along blowups at a smooth center.

papers.title: Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

papers.title: GSPIM: A Temporal-Locality-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting Accelerator with Polymorphic PIM and Multi-Frame Rendering Dataflow
papers.abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) enables high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis for dynamic scenes, supporting free-viewpoint video, mobile XR, and autonomous systems at the edge. Methods using explicit 4D distributions, keyframe interpolation, or anchor binding share two GPU data-movement bottlenecks. Temporal filtering follows model record loading, wasting LPDDR5 bandwidth on inactive data. Frame-isolated execution also overlooks highly overlapping active sets and depth relationships across adjacent frames, reloading shared attributes when working sets exceed on-chip cache capacity. To address these bottlenecks, we present GSPIM, a temporal-locality-aware 4DGS accelerator for PIM-enabled edge devices. Polymorphic PIM adapts a shared near-memory datapath to representation-specific field layouts and selection procedures. It filters and compacts valid data into contiguous inputs before the GPU accesses complete attributes, reducing ineffective transfers. Multi-Frame Rendering Dataflow reuses active attributes and stable depth relationships within a temporal window, reducing repeated work across frames. Hybrid Dataflow Scheduling overlaps near-memory data preparation with GPU rendering to reduce waiting. Evaluation combines a GPU-PIM model calibrated to Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB with a 1z DRAM physical implementation of the added circuits. Across three 4DGS methods and six dynamic scenes, GSPIM achieves a 4.15x geometric-mean speedup and a 4.99x geometric-mean energy-efficiency improvement over a fully optimized frame-by-frame GPU baseline. The maximum scene-level PSNR difference is 0.011 dB, and the added physical footprint is 18.7172 square millimeters across 32 LPDDR5 dies.

papers.title: Exploring the Power Consumption of ERC-4337 Bundling on Server Infrastructure
papers.abstract: The Ethereum ecosystem offers the most widespread support for Decentralised Applications (DApps), with over 120 networks currently documented as using variants of the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) for core execution logic. The ERC-4337 standard provides convenient access to DApps for users who do not possess the required cryptocurrency or prefer flexible authorisation of DApp actions. The infrastructure for ERC-4337 implementation can be deployed on any EVM network. However, to aggregate user requests and submit them to the EVM network, ERC-4337 requires operating a bundler, an additional component. Recently, the potential use of ERC-4337 was boosted by another standard, EIP-7702, which can enable ERC-4337 utility for any existing user account. However, the use of the combined EIP-7702/ERC-4337 pattern remains considerably low at less than 6% of EIP-7702 activity. We believe that this underutilisation is at least partly caused by the low number of existing bundling services and their popularity, currently fewer than 15 publicly documented. Expanding the number of bundler nodes would benefit the ecosystem but would introduce operational costs, part of which is represented by the added nodes' power consumption. In this paper, we provide a thorough view of the bundling power consumption aspect using server-grade infrastructure, evaluating both CPU and RAM consumption, as well as the overhead of container-based deployments specific to production environments.

papers.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
papers.abstract: We propose an interaction-driven route to Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial noninteracting bands in a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and an attractive Hubbard interaction. The large Zeeman splitting renders the noninteracting bands topologically trivial and suppresses spin-flip hopping. These otherwise off-resonant spin-flip processes are resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, generating occupation-dependent spin-orbit coupling that coherently couples neighboring spin-down fermion pairs to onsite doublons. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold ${}^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results provide a route to Weyl superfluidity enabled by interaction-assisted spin-orbit coupling, without requiring nontrivial single-particle band topology.

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moiré Flat-Band Superlattices
papers.abstract: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moiré superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moiré modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moiré superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moiré superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

papers.title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning
papers.abstract: [Note, November 2026: the experimental results in this version are affected by implementation issues in the simulation environment and should not be relied upon pending correction. See the author note on page 1.] An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. We introduce LUCA, a configurable synthetic world for evaluating this process under fully known ground truth. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. This setup allows us to evaluate experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention separately. Across seven frontier LLMs and three baselines, these capabilities dissociate sharply. Agents frequently rescue malfunctioning systems while diagnosing the wrong fault; diagnosis varies 7x across models while prediction varies only 1.4x. Models also adopt surprisingly different experimental strategies, and greater exploration does not reliably yield better performance. In one failure mode, agents often perform the experiment needed to distinguish competing causes, but still fail to use the resulting evidence. LUCA turns these hidden failures into measurable behaviours, providing a controlled environment to study where experimental agents succeed and fail. Code: https://github.com/RelationRx/luca.

papers.title: Operator Fejér-Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial $F\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)[x]$ positive semidefinite on $K$ admits a certificate in the operator quadratic module generated by $S$, with weighted degree at most $\operatorname{deg} F+c_S$. Here, $c_S$ depends only on $S$ and is independent of both $F$ and the coefficient Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, which may be infinite-dimensional. In contrast to the scalar case, natural matrix preorderings admit no uniform degree bound over compact semialgebraic subsets of the real line. We construct positive semidefinite quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees tend to infinity as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap remains bounded below. Conversely, uniform degree bounds hold for interval unions in a fixed compact interval when the component and gap lengths are bounded below by positive constants. Our proofs develop two techniques. The first is a quadratic reduction principle that reduces the problem of obtaining degree bounds for arbitrary-degree operator polynomials to the quadratic case, with a fixed additive increase in degree. The second uses a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil to transfer positivity on unions of intervals to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér-Riesz theorem provides certificates. We also obtain operator-valued Fejér-Riesz factorizations on unions of circular arcs, rational certificates with a fixed denominator on unbounded semialgebraic sets, and a characterization of the sets whose natural operator preorderings admit degree-preserving certificates.

papers.title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the MoS$_2$/Sapphire System
papers.abstract: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the MoS$_2$/ $α$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) system. The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from ~1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On 2,820 held-out test structures from the DFT pool, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/angstrom. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5 %, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of point defects (Spearman $ρ$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($ρ$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($ρ$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %.

papers.title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
papers.abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

papers.title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.

papers.title: Spectra of stochastic matrices with a Toeplitz interior
papers.abstract: For stochastic matrices of order $n$, the Karpelevič region is the set of all possible eigenvalues. We study matrices whose first and last $m$ rows are arbitrary probability vectors, while the remaining rows have a Toeplitz pattern. As $m$ increases, their eigenvalue regions expand, first reaching the full Karpelevič region at $m=\lceil(n-1)/4\rceil$ for $n\ge3$. Reproducing every complete stochastic spectrum, with multiplicities, requires $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. For a boundary arc whose endpoints have orders $q<s$ as roots of unity, the least $m$ needed to attain the whole arc is $0$ for $q=1$ and $\left\lceil\frac12\left\lfloor n/q\right\rfloor\right\rceil$ for $q\ge2$. For a Karpelevič boundary arc whose nonreal points between the endpoints first occur as stochastic eigenvalues at order $n\ge4$, fixing any one of these eigenvalues fixes the characteristic polynomial of every stochastic matrix of order $n$ with that eigenvalue. For these arcs and $m\ge1$, our family attains either the whole arc or only its endpoints. Further results describe the smaller eigenvalue regions and the angles at which their boundaries approach roots of unity.

papers.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents play an important role in solving complex and sustained tasks, with ever-growing interaction contexts. However, these accumulated contexts will raise substantial computational cost and obscure key decision-relevant evidence. Existing methods typically train external compressors or context-management agents to rewrite context as shorter hard-token sequences, but such external selection may not align with the LLM's evolving representation and is necessarily lossy. In this paper, we introduce Agentic Soft-Token Compression (ASTC), a training-free compression method using soft tokens within LLM agent for long-horizon tasks. Specifically, ASTC uses the model's native recurrent dynamics to determine the already absorbed information, leveraging the commonly-used hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention. It then carries this information forward as agentic soft tokens while retaining exact values as hard tokens. The resulting compact sequence reduces later-layer computation and yields reusable KV caches, extending the savings across the agent's trajectory. Extensive experiments on long-horizon tasks show that ASTC matches or exceeds the uncompressed agent's accuracy with up to 59.84% fewer end-to-end Attention Pairs, while trained compressors require 12.3 to 194.9 times more Attention Pairs per successful task. These findings highlight agentic soft tokens as a model-native way to carry absorbed context forward as the task representation evolves.

papers.title: Yesterday's Code, Today's Dependencies: How Dependency Selection Shapes PHP Migration Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Migration benchmarks need projects whose tests pass before migration begins. Yet an old project can behave differently without any change to its code. Reinstalling it today may introduce newer libraries, changing both its initial test results and the failures observed during migration. We investigate this effect in PHP 7.4-to-8.3 migration. Using unchanged project source and saved package records, we compare two dependency policies. Modern selection allows all versions in the snapshot, while release-date selection allows only versions published by the project's release date. With Composer 2 fixed, release-date selection improves the PHP 7.4 pass rate by 7.1 pp across 3,660 releases. A separate comparison against committed locks shows that it also recovers recorded dependency versions more closely than modern selection. The choice matters after migration as well. Among projects that pass on PHP 7.4 under both policies, PHP 8.3 test outcomes differ in 15.0% of eligible pairs. We use a shared test runner and bypass Composer's platform check to isolate test behavior. The resulting candidate migration task sets overlap by only 58.5%. Most differences arise in Laravel projects, where older dependencies trigger deprecations that newer versions avoid. Targeted interventions show that removing these initial failures can restore passing tests or expose further incompatibilities. Thus, dependency selection changes not just whether an old project passes, but also which migration failures a benchmark can observe. Preserved locks provide the strongest available version reference; without them, release-date selection offers a historically grounded alternative. Migration benchmarks should make this choice explicit and report its effect on their results.

papers.title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing a meson parton distribution function (PDF) or parton distribution amplitude (PDA) at a fixed scale from a finite set of Mellin moments. At finite moment order this map is ill posed in the Hadamard sense: the moments do not determine a unique, stable pointwise $x$-dependence, and small data perturbations can produce large changes in the reconstruction. We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.

papers.title: Illusory Truth or Salient Anomaly? Model-Dependent Responses to Repeated Poisoned Passages in RAG-Style Contexts
papers.abstract: Repeated passages in retrieved evidence may influence how language models identify misinformation, even when those passages restate a single underlying claim rather than provide independent support. We compare four instruction-tuned models on 200 claims from the BEIR SciFact test split using paired, fixed seven-document contexts. The minority condition contains one poisoned document and six non-target documents, whereas the majority condition contains the original poisoned document, five paraphrases, and one non-target document. Poison detection rates increase from 45.5% to 66.0% for Apertus-8B and from 4.0% to 15.5% for Aya-Expanse-8B, but decrease from 80.0% to 47.5% for Mistral-Nemo and from 25.0% to 9.5% for Gemma-3-12B-IT. All four paired comparisons are statistically significant. These contrasting results suggest that repeated poisoned evidence does not affect all models in the same way. One possible interpretation is that repetition makes the poisoned claim more conspicuous to some models, potentially facilitating its detection, while other models may treat repeated formulations as reinforcing evidence, potentially reducing their ability to identify the poisoned claim. Although these interpretations require further investigation, the findings highlight the importance of model-dependent responses to repeated evidence in retrieval-augmented settings.

papers.title: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach
papers.abstract: The choice of mixer is central to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), yet no single structural measure captures every limitation of a shallow circuit. We study two complementary properties: configuration-space transport, which constrains probability concentration, and finite-depth causal reach, which limits the problem information available to local observables. In the transport analysis, first-order bounds in the small-$β$ and small-$γ$ regimes reduce to the same cost-weighted Dirichlet energy on connected regular mixer graphs. A non-perturbative $\ell_1$-spreading bound also gives a problem-dependent restriction on the expected objective and on the spreading required for a target approximation ratio. For MaxCut, we augment the transverse-field mixer with graph-aligned two-qubit interactions and establish a causal-radius bound of $(k+1)p$ at depth $p$. Numerical experiments at $k=1$ on cycles, circular ladders, and high-girth regular bipartite graphs show higher best-found approximation ratios for $X+XX$ and $X+YY$ than for standard $X$ at equal depth. Although these augmentations have the same causal-radius bound, $X+YY$ performs better in every tested setting, highlighting the role of operator structure alongside causal reach.

papers.title: Countable unions of intervals without Riesz spectra
papers.abstract: We prove that every set $S = \bigcup_{n = 0}^{\infty} [ t_{2 n + 1} , t_{2 n} )$, where $t_0 > t_1 > \cdots > 0$ and $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} t_n = 0$, admits no Riesz spectrum, that is, no system of exponentials is a Riesz basis for $L^2 ( S )$. Up to a reflection and a null set, this class contains the example of Kozma, Nitzan, and Olevskii (2023). Moreover, combining with the result of Kozma and Nitzan (2015), we show that a bounded countable union of pairwise disjoint intervals of positive length whose endpoints have exactly one accumulation point admits a Riesz spectrum if and only if it is a finite union of intervals up to a null set.

papers.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
papers.abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.

papers.title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items. However, randomly initialized SID token embeddings and GR models trained from scratch do not directly inherit the semantic relations inherent in items, while inter-item collaborative relations are learned largely implicitly through token-level attention and next-token supervision. To address this limitation, we propose REGER, a unified framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation. We pretrain the GR model through generative semantic retrieval, enabling it to inherit inter-item semantic similarity by learning to generate semantic neighbors' SIDs. We combine global attention with local attention aligned with SID boundaries to capture historical context and directed transitions between adjacent items. We formalize item-level preference distillation on the SID prefix tree, deriving an exact factorization of item preference distributions into prefix conditionals and a weighted decomposition of item-level KL divergence into conditional KL terms. Guided by this decomposition, we renormalize the generator's probabilities over legal next tokens and match the resulting distributions to the teacher's conditional preferences along the ground-truth SID path, jointly optimizing the distillation objective with cross-entropy. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed preference distillation and demonstrate that REGER consistently outperforms existing GR baselines while retaining efficient inference.

papers.title: TRUCO: A Scalable Lock-Free Algorithm for Parallel Contour Extraction
papers.abstract: Extracting binary contours and their containment hierarchy is a fundamental step in many computer vision pipelines. While the standard Suzuki--Abe algorithm is inherently sequential, existing parallel tracers neither preserve its exact contours nor compute their hierarchy. This paper presents TRUCO (Threaded Raster Unrestricted Contour Ownership), a lock-free parallel algorithm for multi-core CPUs that produces the exact output of Suzuki--Abe. TRUCO relies on two core ideas. First, the image is partitioned into horizontal stripes, and a geometric ownership rule allows each thread to trace complete contours independently across stripe boundaries, avoiding both locks and post-processing merges. Second, contour tracing is decoupled from hierarchy reconstruction, which is performed in a subsequent parallel pass and can be skipped entirely when only the contours are needed. We formally prove that TRUCO is deterministic, data-race-free, and identical in output to Suzuki--Abe regardless of thread count. Across diverse high-resolution datasets-from sparse segmentation masks to dense real-world photographs-TRUCO achieves speedups of 4.7x to 17.4x over the fastest sequential baseline with hierarchy computation, and 2.3x to 17.8x without it.

papers.title: History of Turn-Ons - the irregular 35-day clock - of Hercules X-1
papers.abstract: Hercules X-1 and Centaurus X-3 are the first ever detected - and as such identified - binary X-ray pulsars. Here we concern ourselves with the 35-day flux modulation of Her X-1, immediately found at its discovery, together with the binary period of 1.7 days and the pulsation with 1.24 s. The 35-day flux modulation shows two flux maxima, the so-called Main-On and the Short-On (with reduced flux). As noticed early on, the period, or the length of the cycle, is variable. The system constitutes an irregular clock, with a more or less stable mean period of near 34.85 d. We consider the repeated rapid increases of the flux from the off-state to the Main-On (the socalled Turn-Ons) as the best timing marker to study this clock. Here we present a complete list of Turn-On times over 55 years, from the discovery of Her X-1 to today (2026), based on historic work from the literature and on observational data provided by five monitoring instruments. We identify to following basic features of the irregular 35-day clock: The Turn-Ons show preference to occur at orbital phases 0.25 and 0.75. The duration of the 35-day cycle clusters around three discrete values - 20.0, 20.5 and 21.0 orbital cycles with a dominant peak at 20.5 Porb (57%). The long-term trend in the 35-day period duration is seen in the O-C (Observed minus Calculated) diagram. There are two sections, separated by the long Anomalous Low of 1999/200 (AL3), which can be modeled by parabolic functions with a smooth evolution of the 35-day period. A medium-term variation is observed in the form of Anomalous Lows, an essential shut-off (at least of soft) X-rays. We find an apparent underlying period of 5.4 yr. There are short-term (hundreds of days) variations (in part quasi-periodic) overlaid to the long-term trend. Straight ups and downs in the O-C diagram, demonstrating rather rapid 35 day period changes.

papers.title: The Great Chat in the Sky: Aligning Exotic Astronomical Data to Language with AstroBridge
papers.abstract: Astronomical observations include images, spectra, and light curves, while the scientific literature describes these objects in natural language. We present AstroBridge, a framework that connects these observations to an LLM through a literature-assisted caption generation pipeline. We used catalog metadata to match observations with scientific texts that describe the same objects. A vision-language model generates descriptive captions from representations of observations, matched passages, and available metadata, creating observation-caption pairs without manual captioning. We train AstroBridge to predict captions directly from raw observations. Modality-specific frozen encoders extract representations that a shared, trainable fusion network aligns with the embedding space of an LLM. In caption-based evaluation of spectra, AstroBridge achieves 91.5% accuracy in distinguishing quasars from galaxies, compared to 69.0% from the base model prior to fine-tuning. Limitations remain in galaxy morphology, classification of minority supernova classes, and the factual quality of generated captions. We believe that AstroBridge's framework is a step towards the goal of aligning the totality of astronomy's diverse, exotic data through the lingua franca of text.

papers.title: Reconstructing False Alarm and Detection Rates in Quantum Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: Published results in quantum machine learning for intrusion detection (QML-IDS) require joint interpretation of false-positive rate (FPR), attack true-positive rate (TPR), and evaluation provenance. We reconstruct operating points in the 25-entry frame selected by Kaissar and colleagues: 21 included articles, 20 identified documentary families, substantive methodological material consulted for 15, and 24 descriptive points from five. In one test-labelled comparison, a quantum support vector machine reduces FPR from 6.875% for random forest to 3.329%, while TPR decreases from 93.955% to 93.682%; both rates improve against three other comparators. In another study, a complete benign row identifies FPR as 12/6000 (0.200%), despite incomplete attack-side allocation that requires additional assumptions for TPR. Normalized matrices identify detection ranges rather than a unique aggregate rate. A uniform provenance rule separates training-described and test-adjusted results from six conditional illustrations whose independence remains unverified. The contribution is a reproducible interpretation of favorable comparisons and detection trade-offs, without converting descriptive results or hypothetical calculations into operational guarantees.

papers.title: A discontinuous Galerkin method for biharmonic Dirichlet control problems with patch reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for Dirichlet boundary control problems governed by the biharmonic equation, with the control imposed through the normal derivative. The method is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation that admits an arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element. We construct a discretization that approximates the state and adjoint state in this space and derive a priori error estimates in the energy and $L^2$ norms. The analysis is carried out under the limited regularity available on polygonal domains by means of a medius argument. Numerical experiments are provided to support the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: On the Characterization Problem for Krull Monoids with Homocyclic Class Group
